Where does Kane rank among all-time England greats?
- Published
Harry Kane is now England's most-capped men's player as well as his country's record goalscorer, but harder to quantify is where these achievements place him among the Three Lions' greatest ever players.
This is a tricky debate with so many variables and a timescale as old as the game itself and, to my mind, not merely a determination of a player's individual ability but also a measure of their impact upon the nation's psyche.
Ballon d'Or winners Stanley Matthews, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen would surely have a shout if the criteria was such, not to mention genius technicians such as Glenn Hoddle, Chris Waddle and John Barnes.
Likewise, if any England boss managed to extract the best from Paul Scholes, Steven Gerrard and Frank Lampard they would be surely making a classic late dart from midfield.
But to qualify as one of the greatest England players of all time, you need the above ability combined with an impactful overall contribution - those memorable moments and an element of longevity - in a Three Lions shirt.
It might be controversial then to leave out Geoff Hurst, who produced the most recognisable performance in England history, while the man he replaced, Jimmy Greaves, would be a shoo-in were it not for injury earlier in the tournament.
It is also hard to rank the contribution of those whose best football came outside of major tournaments and before the dawn of continental competitions - see Eddie Hapgood, Tom Finney, Nat Lofthouse, Dixie Dean et al.
There are only 10 spots, after all, so here we go.
10. David Beckham
Spice Boy. Celebrity. Galactico. There is no argument David Beckham is one of the most iconic England players of all time, but he backed it up on the pitch, too.
Beckham was the face of the Three Lions for a generation, and to his credit managed to overcome the vicious fallout of his red card against Argentina in 1998.
At times he seemed to single-handedly carry England, most notably scoring a 93rd-minute free-kick against Greece to qualify for the 2002 World Cup.
Beckham's former team-mate Gary Neville called him the "most influential player out of England in transforming football".
It's true. On top of 115 caps, Beckham was part of Manchester United's 1999 Treble-winning outfit - finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up - before joining Real Madrid.
His profile was truly global with spells at LA Galaxy, AC Milan and Paris St-Germain.
9. Paul Gascoigne
There's arguably no England star fans forged an emotional attachment with more than Gazza - crying with him in 1990, rejoicing in his spectacular effort against Scotland and desperately willing him to connect during that Euro 96 semi-final defeat by Germany.
Gascoigne won 57 caps and scored 10 goals. At his peak, he was captivating - transcending football as a cultural phenomenon during the summers of '90 and '96, having joined a star-studded Serie A between those tournaments.
Creative, unpredictable, vulnerable. He was a loveable but flawed genius.
He suffered long-term injuries as England missed out on Euro 92 and the World Cup in the USA, but helped the Three Lions qualify for France 98 before being dropped from the final squad, famously wrecking boss Glenn Hoddle's office.
8. Billy Wright
Goalscorers often grab the headlines but I've tried to credit players across positions and eras. From a defensive point of view Ashley Cole, arguably England's best-ever full-back, was close to making it.
But instead it's the great Billy Wright, the first men's player to surpass a century of international caps, including a remarkable 70 successive appearances over eight years.
Wright captained his country on 90 occasions, a joint-record recently broken by Kane, taking in three World Cups with impressive longevity for his era.
He was a true one-club man, winning three league titles, the FA Cup and becoming unofficial "world champions" with Wolves in 1954 - helping inspire the birth of the European Cup - while finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up to Alfredo di Stefano in 1957.
7. Jude Bellingham
It feels a little premature to include a 23-year-old with the bulk of his England career ahead of him, but that shows the impact Jude Bellingham has already made for England and Real Madrid.
A Champions League winner, the midfielder has also appeared at four major tournaments for the Three Lions, becoming the youngest player to do so at the delayed Euro 2020, aged 17.
But his role in helping carry England to the final two years ago and a third-place finish at last summer's World Cup really make him stand out.
Bellingham has delivered those moments a nation collectively remembers. The last-gasp overhead kick against Slovakia in 2024, a quickfire double at the Azteca against Mexico this summer and 93rd-minute quarter-final winner against Norway.
His seven goals at this World Cup were more than any previous Three Lions player in a single edition, the solo effort against France a thing of beauty.
The former Birmingham and Dortmund man doesn't turn 24 until June but has already collected 61 England caps and netted 14 times. As Roy Keane put it, Bellingham has the potential to be one of the "greatest of all time".
6. Wayne Rooney
In terms of natural ability, Wayne Rooney is among England's greatest ever talents.
Bursting on to the scene at Euro 2004 as an electric 18-year-old, having become England's youngest player and scorer the previous year, convinced fans and media the teen sensation could carry the Three Lions to glory in Portugal.
He bounced World Cup winner Lilian Thuram around in England's opener against France in a glimpse of his precocious strength, before scoring twice against both Switzerland and Croatia.
Who knows how far England would have gone had Rooney not been injured against Portugal in the quarter-final?
He was unable to replicate the impact of his first Euros - a red card at World Cup 2006, suspension for the Euro 2012 group stage, seven goals across six major tournaments - but was an all-rounder who brought more than just goals.
Rooney also won it all with Manchester United, becoming the club's all-time top scorer, and finished his 15-year England career with 53 goals from 120 caps.
5. Gordon Banks
There has to be a place for a goalkeeper, and Gordon Banks is the safest pair of hands.
A World Cup winner in 1966, his save from Pele four years later against Brazil is one of the most iconic of all time. Pele called him a "goalkeeper with magic".
Banks spent the majority of his career at Leicester and Stoke, winning a League Cup with each, and earned 73 England caps overall between 1963 and 1972.
His incredible athleticism and reflexes saw the shot-stopper named Fifa's best goalkeeper for five successive years between 1966 and 1971.
4. Gary Lineker
Gary Lineker's early club career did not deliver the silverware as his goals deserved, netting 40 times but finishing league and FA Cup runner-up in his one season at Everton before joining Barcelona.
He scored a Clasico hat-trick and won the Copa del Rey and Cup Winner's Cup, however, before adding an FA Cup with Tottenham in 1991.
Lineker netted 283 club goals (and famously no cards) in total across spells with Leicester, Everton, Barcelona, Spurs and Nagoya Grampus Eight.
But as a player Lineker is most renowned for his contribution in an England shirt, winning the Golden Boot as they reached the World Cup quarter-finals in 1986 - finishing Ballon d'Or runner-up that year - before netting another four as the Three Lions reached the semi-finals in 1990.
Lineker equalised against West Germany before England crashed out on penalties.
However, having missed a spot-kick against Brazil, he finished one short of Bobby Charlton's elusive goal record when his international career ended after Euro 92.
3. Harry Kane
Harry Kane is undoubtedly England's most important and influential player of a generation - it is hard to imagine how this Three Lions side functions once the skipper hangs up his boots.
The Bayern Munich striker, complete with Ballon d'Or, has been scoring goals for his country for almost 12 years, the first just 79 seconds into his debut after coming off the bench against Lithuania in March 2015.
Rooney's goalscoring benchmark is long in his rear view mirror - you wouldn't bank against Kane doubling his nearest rival's figure once his England days are over.
They have come on the biggest stage, too - 21 in 36 appearances from three World Cups and European Championships apiece, winning the World Cup Golden Boot in 2018.
Kane has come closer to winning a major tournament than any England men's captain since Bobby Moore - losing two World Cup semi-finals and back-to-back Euros finals. Team-mate Bellingham called him the "greatest player that has ever played for England".
"I think we'll appreciate him even more in another 10, 15, 20 years when you look back and see what he has achieved," said ex-England goalkeeper Paul Robinson.
2. Bobby Moore
In many ways, Bobby Moore would be the complete modern-day defender. Cool as you like under pressure, elegant in possession, a great passing range off both feet and, as his West Ham and England team-mate Geoff Hurst said: "Nobody out-ran him and nobody out-jumped him."
Moore's positioning and timing was perfect, that iconic tackle on Jairzinho at the 1970 World Cup the finest example of his poise and precision when defending.
He was also a composed and influential leader. A player built for the big occasions. England boss Sir Alf Ramsey called him: "My lieutenant on the field, a cool, calculated footballer I could trust with my life."
The Barking-born centre-back won the FA Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup with West Ham but his finest moment was leading England to glory in 1966. He was only 25 at the time, having become his country's youngest captain three years earlier.
In 1970, after the Bogota bracelet incident, Moore was imperious as England reached the quarter-finals before bowing out to West Germany.
It was, however, the final group game against Brazil, the most exciting side on the planet, that produced some of the most recognisable and renowned images in sporting history - not only Moore's tackle and Banks' save but the defender swapping shirts with Pele after the final whistle.
"The greatest defender I ever played against," was the Brazilian's verdict.
1. Sir Bobby Charlton
For more than a generation, Sir Bobby's England goalscoring record remained unmatched. It took 55 years from his 49th and final strike against Colombia in 1970 until Rooney surpassed him with his half century in 2015.
Charlton was, as Alan Shearer put it, "not only a great goalscorer but a scorer of great goals" and played a pivotal part of the Three Lions' World Cup success in 1966, netting three times on the way to the final.
A scampering run from the halfway line followed by a trademark long-range strike into the corner at Wembley gave England's campaign lift-off against Mexico, before he scored twice against Eusebio's Portugal in the semi-finals.
Manager Ramsey called the buccaneering midfielder his "lynchpin" as England triumphed over West Germany in the showpiece and those performances helped Charlton win the Ballon d'Or later that year.
He'd be runner-up in successive years after that, too.
Charlton won 106 England caps and was a star for Manchester United, with Rooney also the one to pip his club-record 249 goals for the Old Trafford outfit.
A survivor of the Munich air disaster on 6 February 1958, which killed 23 people including eight players and three members of the club's staff, Charlton won three league titles, an FA Cup and most poignantly the European Cup in 1968.
"England's greatest ever player," Lineker previously told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He was unique. Wherever you go in the world, even if they didn't speak the language, they knew two words - Bobby Charlton."

FAA allows flights to resume after hours-long ground stop across the US
Transport secretary Sean Duffy blamed the USA's 'incredibly old air traffic control system.'
The Federal Aviation Administration has lifted a nationwide ground stop in the US that brought all flights to a halt for hours, starting in the afternoon of November 13. Hundreds of flights were canceled, thousands that were already flying had been diverted and millions of passengers were stranded as the ground stop went on. After the FAA lifted the suspension at 8:15PM Eastern time, transportation secretary Sean Duffy held a press conference, blaming old equipment — and the Congress' unwillingness to fund their upgrades — for what happened.
Duffy explained that the USA's "incredibly old air traffic control system" malfunctioned. The US still uses TDM telecom, which is a legacy analog telecommunications technology, to transmit information between facilities. Duffy said that its routers got "overloaded with data," and by 3:36PM on the 13th, they started transmitting inconsistent information. The secretary said the equipment that had already been replaced weren't affected, only the old ones. He also clarified that the US didn't lose all communications and radar, but the FAA still decided to ground flights out of an abundance of caution.
"It's going to continue to fail," Duffy told reporters about the country's air traffic control system, according to the New York Times. "How many times does this have to happen for Congress to give the money to fix it?" The FAA has only issued ground stops thrice this century, and this was the second longest after the 9/11 attacks. While the Congress has already given the FAA $12.5 billion to modernize the country's air traffic facilities, Duffy has been trying to secure $30 billion more.
Markwayne Mullin, the secretary of Homeland Security, appeared with Duffy at the conference and said that there was no indication that the communication issues were caused by a cyberattack. Still, he said his agency was "still looking," and Homeland Security is "not going to rule it out." In addition, Mullin clarified that the incident wasn't related to the lengthy outage that took out Microsoft's services for over 24 hours.

A rumor that U.S. President Donald Trump wrote a social media post chastising Vice President JD Vance, including an order to change the vice president's name, circulated in November.
People on social media shared a purported screenshot of a social media post attributed to Trump that claimed, "I'm hereby signing an EXCLUSIVE ORDER legally changing JD Vance's name to JUDAS DISLOYAL VANCE!"
(X user @miribobs)
The alleged post was dated Nov. 5 and inspired readers to reach out about its authenticity. It circulated after Democrats enjoyed major victories in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.
It read in full:
I'm hereby signing an EXCLUSIVE ORDER legally changing JD Vance's name to JUDAS DISLOYAL VANCE!
Nobody gave JD more than President Trump. I took him from the sidelines and gave him the biggest job of his life—and now he thinks he can DOUBLE CROSS THE BOSS and run for President in 2028 without my blessing?
EHHH!
WRONG!
You don't walk into the Trump Family, eat at the table, kiss the ring, and then decide you're the new Boss!
There is only ONE person who can make America Great Again the RIGHT WAY, and everybody knows who that is.
JD, you may have forgotten who made you—but I NEVER forget!
THE PRESIDENT HAS SPOKEN.
The post was fake, however.
A search of the president's Truth Social account and an online archive of his social media posts revealed no such post.
The fake Trump post circulated as an apparent response, likely satirical, to a Nov. 4 X post by Vance addressing the Republican turnout at the polls for the midterm elections. Vance wrote: "The main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026." His post sparked rumors that he's angling for a 2028 bid for the White House.
The engagement metrics displayed on the fake post — 14.3K reposts, 56.7K likes — exactly match those of other debunked Trump posts, suggesting it may have been generated using a template or a fake post generator. Note that the timestamp is written out as "11/5/26," while authentic Truth Social posts show dates written as "Nov 5, 2026."
The president made multiple posts on Truth Social on that date, but nothing about Vance or a rumored bid for the White House.

Airport-style passport and fingerprinting controls are to be introduced at Eurotunnel in an attempt to prevent “short-term and long-term chaos” in Folkestone and Calais.
In a breakthrough for travellers, the European Commission has agreed to a new system in which an “eagle eye” camera system, already used in Rome and Paris airports to supervise fingerprinting and facial imaging, will be used at the border between the UK and France.
Yann Leriche, the chief executive of Getlink, the Eurotunnel owner, said it had tried to replicate the “airport experience” but wanted to go much further.
Instead of getting out of the car and getting biometrics taken at a terminal building, holidaymakers and business travellers will now be greeted with special drive-through terminals in Folkestone and Calais.
Both sides are now equipped with 120 kiosks under the case of an eagle-eye camera that will be monitored by police, similar to e-gates at airports where police are not physically present at each gate.
In the coming weeks, Leriche will meet UK and French authorities presenting a 40-page proposal to allow Eurotunnel to become a “laboratory” for an “intelligent border” using emerging tech and lessons learned from the US and Singapore.
The entry and exit system (EES) requires all third-country citizens including British passport holders to submit fingerprints and facial images as they enter and exit the Schengen area, but has been delayed for years.
EES was supposed to be active across the EU by 9 September, but nine of the 27 EU member states, including France, have yet to be deploy it fully because of continued technical issues.
It has always been a logistical nightmare for Eurotunnel and a potential cause of miles-long tailbacks at the approach to the terminal.
Originally, Getlink had planned to use a tablet to hand to the passengers in their cars to allow them to self-fingerprint and capture a facial image. It also looked at a system involving passengers parking up and going into the terminal to get fingerprinting.
But both models would have required the physical presence of police officers for first-time fingerprinting.
Leriche said: “We told the authorities: it is going to be a mess. Many people are going to the wrong place and you can’t have police jumping from one place to the next to solve the issues. It would also means customers would have a bad experience, particularly at peak time.
“This is not something people in airports experience, but nobody approached this before, thinking we could have an airport experience at the border here. But we said: why not?”
He said that after “many, many discussions” with the European Commission and the French authorities, finally they were “authorised” to trial “eagle-eye cameras” at each kiosk. “The French authorities are also on board because for them it is more efficient, too, so we are all aligned on the trial,” he said.
The trial will last two years, but Eurotunnel hopes the experiment will become permanent.
Each car will be able to pull up to an individual kiosk, with two stands per vehicle to read passports and take fingerprints and facial images. “It will prevent the chaos in the long term and the short term and if the experiment works, as hopefully it will, then it will become permanent,” said Leriche.
He said the company had been inspired by visits to the US/Mexico border controls, where drivers and passengers remain in their cars.
The requirement of having a police officer present each time a first-time passenger, or “primo” as they are known, submits their fingerprints was designed as a safeguard against subterfuge. Criminals, for example, could use a fellow passenger for example with a “clean skin” fingerprint.
Leriche said he had no idea when the system will be introduced by France. “It has been delayed and delayed and delayed, but our kiosks are there, they are can function but the connection with the French system is still not working. It is a question was are asking all the time.”
This week it emerged that the EU had filed a lawsuit against IBM and two other companies involved in the implementation of EES.

Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said his department is awarding up to $4.9 million to prepare for the first U.S. studies of ibogaine for post-traumatic stress disorder, a hard-to-treat condition linked to higher suicide and substance abuse rates among veterans.
The money will not go directly to patient research, Kennedy said, but to lay the groundwork needed to manufacture, dose and design studies of the drug.
Ibogaine is made from a shrub native to West Africa. It can cause intense hallucinations, nausea, vomiting, tremors and sometimes deadly irregular heart rhythms. Ibogaine is currently illegal, in the same ultra-restrictive class as LSD, ecstasy and most other psychedelic drugs.
Veterans organisations and psychedelic advocates contend that ibogaine has great promise for intractable conditions such as PTSD, severe depression and opioid addiction. U.S. research on the drug has essentially been frozen for decades due to ibogaine's restricted status.
Kennedy said the government will receive data and treatment guidance from Beond Inc., a Texas-based company that has treated more than 3,000 patients with ibogaine in Mexico, where the drug is not illegal.
“That is going to allow us to dramatically accelerate the clinical trial process,” Kennedy said. “We’re going to have, I think, a record drug approval process.”
Additional funding awards may explore ibogaine's use for addiction, he said.
Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins, who joined Kennedy for the announcement, said the collaborative effort would focus first on safety and “best-in-class research.”
“For veterans living with PTSD, we owe them both urgency and the best science we can produce,” Collins said.
Kennedy and Collins have previously voiced support for the potential of psychedelics, citing the experiences of veterans who have traveled abroad for therapy with ibogaine and other mind-altering substances.
Thursday's announcement was previewed in April, when Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to speed up review and research of psychedelics that could help with mental health conditions.
Three applications for psychedelics are pending review at the Food and Drug Administration. They include the first potential medicines made from psilocybin, the active ingredient in magic mushrooms, and MDMA, also called ecstasy. Decisions on those drugs could come within weeks or months.
Because of its safety risks, ibogaine research has moved more slowly.
The little data currently available mostly comes from patients who have traveled to Mexico or other countries where ibogaine is not heavily regulated. Ibogaine clinics typically charge $10,000 to $20,000 for one course of treatment, which often involves monitoring of a patient's heart readings while emergency medical workers are on standby.
Trump's order on psychedelics came after podcaster Joe Rogan said he texted Trump about ibogaine, which he repeatedly has discussed on his show. According to Rogan, the president quickly responded: “Sounds great. Do you want FDA approval? Let’s do it.”

In March, Guardian Australia revealed that most people who have been charged with the new federal crime of possession of violent extremist material are under 18.
This week Australian federal police sounded the alarm about a surge in teen extremism: 32 of the 37 young people prosecuted in counter-terrorism cases since 2020 were charged in the past two years.
The growth in youth extremism is happening within a sprawling online ecosystem. My investigations have tracked the rise of online networks that urge violence and nihilism for their own sake, in which perpetrators coerce victims not much younger than themselves to commit brutal and degrading acts.
In a review of 55 youth terrorism cases, the AFP has found that the profile is mixed. They are often young men. Many have received some support or intervention for a mental health condition. Some are from stable homes, others not.
What they have most in common is that they are young people on the internet. Experts say the age of those caught up in these crimes is decreasing.
In the last month two teenagers in Darwin have been charged with collecting documents that could facilitate acts of terrorism.
The arrests came five months after another NT teenager was charged with making posts with “pro-Nazi, anti-immigration, anti-trans and white nationalist themes”. The charge sheet alleges he also possessed videos of white nationalist terrorist attacks, including the 2019 Christchurch mosque shooting and the 2022 Buffalo shooting that it partly inspired.
All matters are still before the courts.
Experts involved in harm prevention programs, including the Victoria University professor Debra Smith, have watched the age of this cohort decrease dramatically over the past decade.
Instead of considering the challenge exclusively through the lens of radicalisation, Smith says we need to recognise that some young people are being socialised and finding identity in online spaces that may appear exciting and transgressive but are ultimately harmful to themselves, and may encourage them to do harm to others.
She has seen cases where teenagers are being found with “hard drives full of what can only be described as gore”.
“It’s like getting involved in any other … unhealthy subcultural aspect of life … [such as] gangs or crime for payment,” she says. “There’s this offering of what young people can look at and get involved in that just simply wasn’t there years ago.”
The Guardian’s investigation into the growth of extremist material charges, as well as the surge of young people in Australia ensnared in sadistic online extortion and gore networks, reveals an amorphous online ecosystem in which young people may easily come into contact with extreme and violent content.
A teenager in New South Wales who pleaded guilty to possessing violent extremist material, among other charges, described how he first came across such content on TikTok when he was 14 and sought validation by talking to others online. He used ChatGPT to research the Boston marathon bomber Dzhokhar Tsarnaev as well as security arrangements at the Sydney Opera House. He was sentenced to a three-year community corrections order.
Others have told police how they became involved in so-called “gore” channels on Telegram, where more and more extreme footage – including of animal abuse – is traded.
Given the age of many involved, Levi West, a research fellow at the Australian National University, says they may be considered as much victims as perpetrators, which is a significant challenge for how authorities respond.
It’s important for parents, schools and others to think about what’s sitting underneath the uptick in numbers, he says, and not just the “algorithms”. He points to the legacies of Covid-19 and lockdowns as well as the presence of screens and digital technologies in the lives of young people.
“We are not going to arrest our way out of this problem,” West says.
With people as young as 13 before the courts, Australia must consider if authorities are taking the right approach and have the right resources for this challenge.
The Guardian’s investigation into the possession of extremist material charges in South Australia and around the country found that many of those who had been before the courts faced a range of health and social difficulties, including autism diagnoses and learning challenges – and raised questions about whether some young people understand a crime has been committed.
Smith has seen many young people caught up in these activities who come from troubled family backgrounds, while others have had every opportunity in life.
There is a role for everyone involved in caring for young people, she says, from parents and schools to sporting clubs, to recognise when someone might be engaging in harmful behaviours long before there is a risk of violence, then help them access non-punitive pathways for help.
“It’s really important to understand it through a developmental lens – that these are young people who are making decisions with young brains,” Smith says.
“My grave concern is that if we are just giving everyone terrorism offences at [age] 12, 13, 14, 15, we’re starting to label them the thing that they will become.”

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has sought details from home services platforms, including Pronto, Snabbit and Urban Company’s InstaHelp, over the collection of first-person video and sensor data from gig workers for training physical AI models. As per a report by ET , a meeting chaired by MeitY secretary S Krishnan yesterday brought together senior executives from the quick home services platforms and other technology and robotics companies to discuss concerns around workers’ consent, consumer privacy and data sovereignty. Officials are concerned that recordings of everyday household activities could infringe workers’ rights, compromise consumer privacy and pose risks to national data security. The ministry sought details on the standard operating procedures (SOPs) followed by companies for collecting, processing and storing such data. It also sought information on safeguards for obtaining workers’ consent and protecting the privacy of other individuals captured in the recordings. The ministry also sought clarity on whether companies were selling, sharing or transferring the collected data to physical AI developers outside India. It asked Pronto to submit details of its data collection practices and the SOPs it follows, ET reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. When asked by Inc42 about the meeting and the details sought by the ministry, Pronto said it had participated in the meeting as part of a broader industry consultation involving home services platforms, robotics companies and other stakeholders. The spokesperson said that the consultation provided an opportunity for the ministry and industry participants to exchange perspectives, share existing practices and discuss the opportunities and challenges emerging from the evolving AI landscape. “Pronto shared its current practices as part of this exchange and looks forward to continued engagement with MeitY and other industry stakeholders,” the startup said. Inc42 has reached out to Snabbit and Urban Company for their comments on the development. The story will be updated upon receiving responses. Concerns were also reportedly raised about India becoming a source of cheap training data for foreign AI companies. Executives suggested that the country should focus on developing its own physical AI capabilities rather than merely supplying data to overseas developers. This comes shortly after Pronto faced scrutiny over a pilot programme to record household chores using cameras worn by service professionals to generate training data for robotics systems. The controversy also brought Snabbit and Urban Company under scrutiny over their potential involvement in this. Snabbit subsequently clarified that it had conducted a limited assessment of the tech in a controlled training-centre environment but decided against proceeding with the proposal. Urban Company founder Abhiraj Singh Bhal said the company neither records inside customers’ homes nor plans to do so. Pronto, meanwhile, confirmed that it was running an opt-in pilot involving first-person video recordings of household chores. Initially, it said the feature was available only to customers who actively opted in during booking and was limited to less than 0.01% of its users. The startup later told Inc42 that raw footage was deleted immediately after the work was completed, while an anonymised, end-to-end encrypted recording remained accessible only to customers for 48 hours. The anonymised footage was subsequently used for AI training, as outlined in its terms. This further casts a shadow on Pronto founder Anjali Sardana's expanding ambitions in physical AI beyond the home services business. In July, the startup formalised its data collection experiment through Verified, an opt-in premium service in which professionals wear head-mounted or body-mounted cameras during visits. Last month, Sardana launched Provision Labs, a San Francisco-based physical AI venture that will collect data to train and test AI systems designed to perform real-world tasks using robots and other machines. Provision Labs also announced the acquisition of Mumbai-based Basilisk Industries, a startup focused on perception technologies. Basilisk founder Shourya Watwani will lead Provision’s hardware efforts and work on its in-house post-processing models. The relationship between Pronto’s household data collection and Provision Labs’ operations remains unclear.

Mumbai: YES Bank has asked the Supreme Court to review its 15 October order upholding a Bombay High Court ruling against the write-down of ₹8,415 crore of additional tier-1 (AT-1) bonds, a move that could prolong the wait for bondholders. “The Bank has filed a review petition under Article 137 of the Constitution of India before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India seeking review of its judgment and order dated October 15, 2026 in relation to the write-down of additional tier-1 bonds aggregating to ₹8,415 crore,” the lender said in a late Friday disclosure to the stock exchanges. In its 15 October ruling, the Supreme Court dismissed appeals by YES Bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Centre, upholding a Bombay High Court order that held that the bank’s administrator had no authority to write down the bonds as part of the lender’s 2020 rescue. The case relates to the perpetual AT-1 bonds that were written down as part of the YES Bank Reconstruction Scheme, 2020. Bondholders and the trustee, Axis Trustee Services, challenged the decision before the Bombay High Court, which quashed the write-down in January 2023. The Supreme court directed YES Bank to restore the bonds to bondholders with immediate effect. However, with the lender yet to act on the judgment, the YES Bank AT-1 Bond Holders Association, which represents around 400-450 affected investors, and Axis Trustee Services have written to the bank seeking restoration of the bonds and payment of pending interest dues. “The bank will take all such steps and measures as are necessary and permissible under applicable law,” including consequential actions, available legal remedies and other steps that may appropriately be taken in accordance with the law, it said in a letter to Axis Trustee dated 30 October. The lender has reiterated the same in other public disclosures, and has also informed stakeholders that it is continuing to evaluate and assess the matter Shares of YES Bank ended 0.3% lower at ₹17.42 on the National Stock Exchange on Friday. Reinstating the bonds is expected to have a significant capital and margin impact for the lender. In the earnings call, managing director and chief executive director Vinay Tonse had said that reinstatement of the AT-1 principal amount is expected to have a pro forma impact of approximately 240 basis points on the bank’s common equity tier-1 ratio, including profits. As of 30 September, the bank’s capital adequacy ratio was 14.5% and the common equity tier-1 ratio was 13.7%. “Our overall Tier 1 capital ratio is expected to remain around 13.7% on a pro forma basis. We recognize that the distinction between CET-1 and overall Tier 1 capital is important. We will continue to assess the implications for our capital structure, regulatory buffers, balance Sheet strength, and future growth plans,” Tonse had said. Takeda reported that its narcolepsy pill, the first treatment to target the underlying cause of the rare sleep disorder, is now available in the U.S. after the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration removed the final regulatory hurdle for its rollout, Reuters notes. The DEA has classified Orzeyful as a Schedule IV controlled substance, a category considered to have a low potential for abuse and dependence. Demand for hormone replacement therapy has been rising, particularly in the U.S., where prescriptions have increased after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration removed long-standing safety warnings a year ago. Some other hormone therapy products to treat menopause symptoms are also facing supply constraints in Canada.

This story is based on an interview with Vanessa Santos, 43, a business consultant for female founders from Phoenix. It has been edited for length and clarity.
I got a message on the app that my 1:45 p.m. Southwest Airlines flight from Phoenix was slightly delayed, giving me a chance to dash to Starbucks.
The delay was longer than expected. Then, as we finally boarded the plane, I overheard the gate agent telling another employee something about a ground stop.
We were told to deplane
A man sitting across from me looked alarmed. "This hasn't happened since 9/11," he said.
We sat at the gate for 45 minutes, then were told to deplane. The announcer said the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) had grounded all US flights.
Nobody was complaining, and the general attitude was that there was nothing we could do about it. However, over time, people began to panic, asking whether they should rebook.
They were trying to open the app, but it wasn't working. Next, someone said it was the result of a cyberattack. The energy changed, and I decided I didn't want to stay there anymore.
I was due to speak at my friend Alexis's business conference the next morning, and I couldn't think of anything worse than letting her down.
It had been months in the making, and she was relying on me.
No rental cars were available
Then I remembered another friend, Marisol, in the city who'd told me she was driving to Vegas. I texted her on the off-chance she hadn't set off. If she had, I would have rented a car.
Fortunately, she was still at home. She said she had room in her Kia SUV for one more person: me. I was so relieved, especially after I discovered that no rental cars were available.
And so began my impromptu road trip. Marisol's husband, Francisco, drove with her up front. Marisol's friend, Jess, and I sat in the back.
I called myself a passenger princess because I felt so spoiled. We stopped at Buc-ee's to pick up snacks and In-N-Out for meat patties.
We sang along to a '90s hip-hop playlist — millennial throwbacks —and had great chats. I would never have experienced that on the plane.
It took six hours
The journey was a cool adventure from start to finish. It rained hard, so we had to pull over several times. It didn't matter. I was getting to Las Vegas against the odds.
All in all, it took seven hours, including breaks, to drive 300 miles to our destination. I was excited to be moderating my panel after all.
It was Friday the 13th, and unlucky for other travelers stranded at the airport. I felt bad for them. For me, however, it was a pretty awesome day.

Hyderabad cricket has heard many speeches, but few came with a tractor.
In the six months since Ambati Rayudu promised to change the culture, the former India batter has been seen at pitch-side at dawn, at the soil vendor’s door in the rain and, by his own count, five to seven kilos lighter.
The initial results suggest the effort is paying off. The first phase of this Ranji Trophy season has wrapped up with Hyderabad winning three matches and playing out one draw, enough to sit on top of the Elite Group B table with 20 points. From players to coaches, the delight is evident.
Rayudu, the Director of Cricket Operations at the Hyderabad Cricket Association, shares it, but he is wary of premature celebrations. He takes his pride instead from the system underneath.
“I wouldn’t read too much into the results as of now, but I’m very happy with the way the systems are set. And most importantly, the boys are very confident and glad there is something to look forward to,” he told Sportstar.
It is a long way from May 5, when he walked into a hall of cameras and vowed to take Hyderabad cricket to the next level. Plenty of men have said as much in those corridors. What followed, Rayudu says, was quieter than the promise: basics, done properly, every single day.
First, he filled the calendar. Hyderabad’s age-group sides now play far more than the league demands, close to a thousand match days this season. It is how his own generation grew up.
“When they wake up, if they don’t have a game, they need to be worried: ‘What am I going to do today?’ We wanted to get that feeling back.”
Wasim Jaffer’s arrival as mentor has reinforced that change, bringing a cricketing culture to players and coaches alike. Open trials now let district players walk into Gymkhana and chase a State cap.
From the grassroots to the selection room, no corner of the system escaped a rethink.
“The first point on our agenda while picking selectors was: Do they have the integrity required? Because beyond that, we will take care of whatever comes. And because they come with such integrity, they are quite adamant and stubborn in their decision making as well. That is a welcome sign because we don’t want them to be yes-men. And they have done a fantastic job, so no complaints at all. All due credit to Jeevan Reddy (HCA secretary) or anybody else, they have never questioned the team selections.”
His Cricket Operations Committee (COC) had only stepped in when choosing who to lead the side.
Every pick and every omission is done through a signed sheet, filed with the Single Member Committee (SMC) headed by retired Justice P. Naveen Rao, Jeevan and the COC.
“The sheets have all the details about why a player was selected. In case any issue comes up, everything can be checked. It’s a way to avert any bad calls. It’s just like a Decision Review System (DRS), which helps us avoid blunders. If something comes up in the future, there is always documentation, which over a few years also helps us gather data on what could have been better.”
Digging in
From a cricket development perspective, Hyderabad’s flat tracks are no one’s first choice. They weren’t Rayudu’s either. International fixtures returning to the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium meant domestic hosting duties were solely granted to the iconic Gymkhana ground in Secunderabad.
Rayudu had ideas, but had to deal with some anticipated roadblocks first.
“There were so many apprehensions. Funds weren’t getting released sometimes. Tenders were not being opened.”
The system dragged its feet but Rayudu and head curator Mukesh Kumar did not. Priority was finding the right soil to redo the pitches.
They waited on vendors who vanished when the rains came, paid extra for earthmovers and chased labour that never turned up. When no tractors could enter the city, Rayudu sent for his own.
ALSO READ | Ranji Trophy 2026-27: “Both stressed and happy,” Anirudh Singh on Hyderabad’s last-gasp win
“Once everything came to the ground, we did not get labour sometimes. There were no tractors that were coming into the city, among other issues. So I brought my own tractor and the person who works on my farm. He is the one who has done all the banks that you see in Gymkhana now.”
Picking the soil, too, was just as elaborate and involved early morning trips to neighbouring districts.
“We’ve put in three types of soil. Even the mixed soil used is a natural mix. The soil near Vikarabad naturally gets mixed with red and black, so that is one of the soils that we picked up. There’s also a black soil pitch which is a proper seaming track which, I am sure, will come in handy in the future.”
His benchmark comes from seven seasons at Motibaug with Baroda. A good Ranji pitch, he explained, lets teams bat about 90 overs and keeps all four innings alive. The toss should not decide the outcome.
This surge was hardly without resistance. Ticking deadlines, noncooperative arms of bureaucracy and funding trouble came and went but the COC persevered. On the field, backing local league performers for the newly introduced Super League places drew backlash from those used to doing it differently.
Rayudu shrugged off the risk. “What is the worst thing that can happen? They would have all signed a petition to remove us! But by the time that happens, we would have already done a lot of good work.”
Rayudu sits now with the satisfaction of a productive start under his belt.
“It was a crazy experience, but we were not going to stop for anybody. It’s not just me. Even Wasim bhai, Mukesh and COC members P.S. Niranjan and M.P. Arjun, they have put in a lot of effort behind the scenes to make all this happen. It’s been a painstaking and stressful one, but for the first time in HCA’s history, I think good is winning over evil.”
Systems to outlast
The next phase moves beyond Gymkhana. Academies have been planned in Mahabubnagar and Karimnagar, along with a high-performance centre at Uppal, possibly run by an outside body under a public-private model. Rayudu hopes to get work started within a month or two. HCA-run teams may also enter different league divisions, so that talent found at open trials has somewhere competitive to play.
Women’s cricket will follow.
“We didn’t have time to go into women’s cricket this season,” Rayudu admitted, adding, “It’s just a matter of time that everything will follow in women’s cricket as well. SMC and even Jeevan are very eager to get everything done in the women’s game as well.”
Less than a decade ago, Rayudu took to social media and did not mince his words in criticising the way HCA was run. And he admitted that he never saw himself coming to bring out the change he longed to see.
“I thought that there was no hope left. But as they say in India, justice is always delayed, but it is never denied. I wouldn’t say things are perfect right now, not at all. There’s still a long way to go from here, but the processes are being set, there are a lot of systems and protocols that have come into place. Eventually at the end of the season we will release a document on the systems and processes. Once it all gets ratified and if followed, a lot of good will happen in the future.”
ALSO READ | Fast bowler needs pace and bounce: Siraj embraces New Zealand challenge
Rayudu, who said his desire is to see HCA among India’s top five associations in administration as well as cricket, said he is taking it all one year at a time. He has had the support of the SMC and Jeevan during this time, something he constantly credits for what he’s managed to do in the opening months of his tenure.
“I told myself that I’ll give everything to Hyderabad cricket for a year. I wanted to sacrifice a year for Hyderabad, which has done so much for me in terms of my cricketing career. Beyond this, I want to set up systems and protocols. The main thing is that SMC needs to be there for at least two or three years. That is very, very important, and along with him Jeevan should be around. I think with them and with these systems, even if I am there or not, it will all run very well.”
It’s been a decade since Hyderabad made the Ranji knockouts. They’ve even had a taste of life in the Plate division since. Three wins in four fixtures is a good start, but it’s just that – a start. Rayudu and his team have picked their Everest. But the first steps look promising.

A video emerged showing the American Heritage river cruise ship sinking into the Mississippi River in New Orleans after colliding with the Atlantic Asphalt tanker on Friday. Passengers can be seen panicking and jumping into the water as the five-storey vessel begins to tilt and eventually goes down. 
Rescue teams, including tugboat operators, dock workers and police personnel, rushed to the scene to pull people from the river.
All passengers and crew aboard the cruise ship were rescued, with no one reported missing. At least 32 people were taken to hospital, but none suffered critical injuries, New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said. Around 180 people, including passengers and crew, were aboard the vessel when the tanker struck it at the Port of New Orleans.
The American Heritage began taking on water and listing sharply within minutes of the collision, triggering a large-scale rescue operation. Dozens of people were pulled from the water, including at least two police officers.
The tanker apparently lost steering before crashing into the docked cruise ship.
"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi,” Moreno said at a news conference, as rescuers and others cheered.
“It was docked right at the Port of New Orleans when a tanker ship lost control and collided into the cruise ship,” Moreno said.
The American Heritage began listing within minutes of the collision and eventually flipped while emergency personnel were still working to evacuate those aboard.
Dozens of passengers and at least two police officers were pulled from the Mississippi River, where the water temperature was around 19 degrees Celsius.
Devon Flanagan, who was working nearby at the Port of New Orleans, said he saw workers rushing towards the dock before noticing that the cruise ship had overturned and passengers were struggling in the water.
“It was just chaos,” he said. “You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water.”
The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have experienced “some type of loss of steering”.
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) was expected to investigate the incident. However, its investigators were initially unable to reach New Orleans after flights across the country were grounded due to communication problems at regional air traffic control centres.
Passengers who were not injured were taken to a nearby auditorium, where cruise officials conducted a roll call to ensure everyone was accounted for, Moreno said.
Many passengers lost their identification documents and car keys during the incident. Most were visitors from outside New Orleans and needed assistance with accommodation, transportation and other basic arrangements.
“They needed chargers for their phones. Some people didn't have phones,” Moreno said. “This has now made national news. They need to contact their families to let them know they're OK. Food, hotel rooms, transportation.”
The American Heritage, operated by American Cruise Lines, was completing an eight-day voyage covering several destinations along the Mississippi River in Louisiana and Mississippi.
Built in 2015, the 160-metre-long vessel can accommodate up to 150 passengers. It was scheduled to end its journey in New Orleans, according to maritime tracking website MarineTraffic.
Martin Davies, a maritime law expert at Tulane University, said it was too early to establish the cause of the collision. However, videos of the incident appeared to indicate a possible catastrophic failure of systems aboard the tanker.
He described the circumstances as “super bad luck” because the collision occurred as passengers were departing the cruise ship.
Davies said the tanker was travelling upriver against the current at a relatively slow speed.
“For something like this to happen for an upbound ship indicates that something must have gone really badly wrong,” Davies said.
He added that tankers generally have local pilots aboard to guide them through waterways because of their familiarity with the river and the vessel. The tanker had also completed the difficult Algiers Point turn on the Mississippi River before the collision.
According to the International Maritime Organisation, the tanker is owned by Nave Shipping SA, a company registered in Monrovia, Liberia. MarineTraffic identifies it as a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, a major Chinese state-owned conglomerate.
The corporation accounted for nearly a quarter of the global commercial shipbuilding market in 2022 and was also the world's largest military shipbuilder at the time, according to a report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.
China State Shipbuilding Corporation did not respond to an emailed request for comment on Friday afternoon.
During his first term, US President Donald Trump listed the corporation among more than two dozen Chinese-owned companies that he accused of exploiting “United States investors to finance the development and modernisation” of the Chinese military.
The executive order did not freeze all economic transactions involving the listed companies but imposed restrictions on the types of transactions they could undertake on US soil.

New Delhi- All Microsoft products became operational on Saturday, the company’s service health page showed, after a massive global outage that disrupted Outlook email and other workplace services, with the firm saying it was deeply sorry and blamed the incident on a network capacity upgrade issue.
The page read “All products are operational” on Saturday morning, including Microsoft 365 (business or enterprise) and consumer products.
“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously,” Microsoft said in a post on X.
The company said the outage was a technical issue and was not related to cyber activity or to AI or agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade, which surfaced following a recent network change, it said.
Microsoft said it has addressed the underlying issue. Given the scale of demand, it restored services gradually and checked stability at each stage, which took longer but helped ensure a stable restoration, the company said.
“Our investigation points to technical challenges and failure modes (cascading failures + thundering herds at our network perimeter) that made recovery more difficult than normal. I’m working closely with the engineering team to complete the full post-mortem. We will publish the post-mortem shortly covering the step-by-step timeline and our many repair items to avoid similar outages in the future,” Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s Executive Vice President of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said in a post on X.
Microsoft’s status account on X said on Saturday that it continued to observe sustained service recovery and was monitoring for an extended period because of the severity of the incident. It said it was also watching the backlog of emails built up during the outage to make sure all of them were processed before it considered the issue resolved.
The outage, which began late on Thursday, had hit Indian airlines, financial services firms, and businesses. Domestic airlines IndiGo, Air India and Akasa Air reported disruptions to email-based customer support, affecting their ability to receive or respond to some passenger queries. Air India temporarily rerouted email services to ensure customer communications continued reaching the airline, while flight operations were not reported to have been affected.
Financial services firms also faced difficulties accessing research reports and conducting client interactions.
The disruption primarily affected Microsoft 365 features that interact with Exchange Online, the company’s cloud-based email platform. Users were unable to access mailboxes through Outlook on the web and desktop applications, and email delivery was delayed.
At its peak, the outage generated more than 1.3 lakh reports of Outlook problems on outage-tracking website Downdetector, with disruptions reported across 72-74 countries.

A Mexican Singer Gives Old Ballads New Heroines
Grammy-nominated songwriter Vivir Quintana is known throughout Latin America for giving voice to women who fought back against domestic violence.
Against the backdrop of a centuries-old stone church in the Mexican city of Oaxaca, the singer Vivir Quintana raised her deep, husky voice above the blare of trumpets, trombones and the booming pulse of a tuba.
Behind her stood a brass band of young Indigenous girls in embroidered white blouses and brightly colored skirts. Hat in hand and fist raised, Ms. Quintana sang a corrido, a traditional Mexican folk ballad usually used to recount tales of revolutionaries, outlaws, folk heroes, and more recently, drug traffickers.
Corridos are typically sung by men, about men. Ms. Quintana sang a corrido she wrote based on the true story of a woman who fought back when her abusive partner tried to gouge out her eyes with a knife.
“I used to think that what united us women was our pain. Now I have realized it is love and resistance,” Ms. Quintana told the crowd in October during a women’s conference in Oaxaca called Decididas, drawing a roar of applause. “We must keep defending ourselves!”
On Thursday, Ms. Quintana will take the stage at the Latin Grammy Awards in Las Vegas alongside the Colombian pop superstar Juanes, with whom she is nominated for song of the year for “Humano.” It is her second Latin Grammy nomination.

In Moscow, Witkoff and Kushner Ask Putin to Include Europe in Peace Talks
The Kremlin, taking a hard line, is pushing to widen negotiations to overhaul European security structures.
President Trump’s envoys went to Moscow on Thursday to seek agreement from President Vladimir V. Putin to bring Europe into talks on the war in Ukraine, as the Kremlin pushes to widen the negotiations to overhaul European security arrangements.
The envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, arrived in Russia one day after mediating peace talks in Abu Dhabi between Russian and Ukrainian representatives, who spoke directly for the first time in nine months. After meeting with Mr. Putin in the Kremlin, the envoys were scheduled to travel to Dublin to meet with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine.
Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner are pressing to involve Europe in the talks as Russia makes clear that it will not consider a cease-fire until its broader demands to redraw the European security architecture are addressed.
The Trump administration, seeking a foreign policy win after Republicans’ drubbing in the midterm elections, is making another push for peace even as Russia gives no indication that it will stop the war anytime soon, and in fact appears to be hardening some of its positions.
Russia has intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities ahead of a winter bombing campaign, taking advantage of Ukraine’s lack of air defenses. On Thursday, Mr. Zelensky said that the Ukrainian armed forces were again facing restrictions on Starshield, the military version of the satellite internet network Starlink, and had asked the United States for information.

Delhi NCR-based gaming startup Zupee has nothing more to lose. For one, it has laid off its entire workforce. Then, its announcement of a pivot towards AI has failed to see the light of day. According to sources, the startup has provided severance pay to the affected employees, covering the period until January 2027, and its October pivot was a veiled attempt to present the impending closure. The final round of layoffs coincided with Zupee’s public announcement of its foray into AI, Inc42 has learnt. On October 16, the startup said it was positioning its existing technological capabilities as the foundation for its AI ambitions. However, it did not disclose its new gig. Further, the October layoffs followed two earlier rounds of job cuts. Zupee sacked around 200 employees 10 months before its October layoff and nearly 170 employees before that. At its peak, the startup employed close to 500 employees. Inc42 reached out to Zupee for comment but did not receive a response. Zupee Disguises Shutdown? On October 16, Zupee announced that it was exiting the gaming business and would focus on building AI-led ventures. The ailing startup said it would leverage its experience of serving over 200 Mn users to develop AI products for Indian consumers. “There was no AI plan. It was a damage control exercise to hide the fact that Zupee was winding down its operations. Currently, they have no employees left, barring 3-4 who are working with the founders,” sources told Inc42. Meanwhile, Zupee has also shut down its astrology platform, NeoAstro, and its microdrama venture, Zupee Studio, as part of its restructuring in October. The closure of these businesses suggest that Zupee may have already been winding down. Zupee entered the microdrama segment as part of this diversification strategy. It was in advanced discussions to acquire Vertical TV. “However, the proposed acquisition eventually fell through,” sources said. Inc42 could not independently ascertain the reasons behind this. What Happens To Zupee's $120 Mn Warchest? Founded in 2018 by Dilsher Singh Malhi and Siddhant Saurabh, Zupee built its business around mobile versions of traditional Indian games, including Ludo, Snakes and Ladders and Carrom. Over the years, it had raised over $120 Mn from investors, including Z47, Orios Venture Partners, Nepean Capital, WestCap Group, Tomales Bay Capital and AJ Capital. With its gaming business discontinued and its other consumer ventures reportedly shut down, questions remain about the startup’s remaining cash reserves, assets and outstanding liabilities. Inc42 reached out to Zupee’s investors, including Z47 Partners and Nepean Capital, to understand whether they were informed about the impending shutdown and workforce reduction, and whether the AI pivot was presented to them as a genuine business strategy. Investors have also been asked about the current status of their investment, the possibility of recovering unutilised capital and whether the management has initiated discussions around a potential shutdown or liquidation. However, none of the investors responded to Inc42’s queries. For a startup that raised close to $120 Mn and built a consumer platform with a claimed user base of over 200 Mn, the developments mark a significant reversal from its earlier growth ambitions.

- There are a total of 9 NPCs in Fortnite Treasure Hunters.
- NPCs in Fortnite Treasure Hunters can be hired to aid you or open a Rift for you and your party.
- Epic will add more NPCs to the Fortnite Treasure Hunters map as the storyline progresses.
Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season has introduced several new NPCs to the island, with two being carried over from Chapter 7 Override. Each of them has a story to tell and offers some service. That said, here’s where to find all NPCs in Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season and what to expect from them.
All Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season NPC Locations and Services
There are a total of 9 NPCs in Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season, with most of them being centered in and around POIs. You have to eventually visit all of them, be it to complete quests or merely to explore the entirety of the Fortnite Treasure Hunters map.
Unlike the bosses in Fortnite Treasure Hunters, you can approach these NPCs without the fear of being attacked. They are friendly and do not attack unless provoked. That said, here is where to find all Fortnite Treasure Hunters NPCs and what they provide in terms of services:
| NPC Name | Location | Services Offered | 
|---|---|---|
| Treasure Hunter Hope | Lantern Landing | Hire | 
| Charlotte-Sensei | The $.$. Rocky | Hire | 
| Buccaneer Brigand Jones | Windmill Village | Hire | 
| Kawaii Team Leader | Lil’ Uzi’s Stronghold | Hire | 
| Nami | South of Windmill Village | Rift | 
| Roronoa Zoro | Arlong Park | Rift | 
| Monkey D. Luffy | Loguetown | Rift | 
| Sanji | Busy Bay | Rift | 
| Usopp | Loguetown | Rift | 
Out of the 9 NPCs in Fortnite, only 4 of them can be hired to aid you in combat. If you plan on hunting for new Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season, it’s always good to have more party members. The rest provide a “Rift” service, which is used to rotate. That said, we’ve provided a map to help you get a better idea of where they are located.
Keep in mind that the list of NPCs in Fortnite Treasure Hunters can change as the Mini Season progresses. However, as of the Fortnite Treasure Hunters update 43.10, this is where each NPC can be found on the island.
How to Hire an NPC in Fortnite
You can hire one NPC per player, for a total of three when playing in a squad. With the Fortnite Pirate Shop benefiting the entire team, playing together now makes more sense. That said, follow these steps to hire an NPC in Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season:
- Check the map to see where the NPC is located and go to the general area.
- Once you are near an NPC that can be hired, look for the hire marker on top of the NPC’s head to confirm it’s a hireable NPC.
- Approach and talk to the Fortnite NPC using the interact button (E on the keyboard, Square on PlayStation, X on Xbox).
- Click on “Hire NPC” and confirm the service.
Once you hire the NPC, they follow you around wherever you go. Keep in mind that they can get eliminated, so try to protect them as best you can. They are rather nifty during a Battle Royale match, especially if you’re trying to complete One Piece Quests in Fortnite.
Where Did Gold Bars Go in Fortnite?
By now you’ve probably noticed that you don’t need to spend Gold Bars to hire an NPC or use any service since they’re all free. Epic Games has officially vaulted Gold Bars as of Fortnite update 43.00. This is rather odd since the theme is “Treasure Hunters” and everyone revolves around loot.
That’s about everything you need to know about NPCs in Fortnite Treasure Hunters. Remember to visit them as soon as you can to hear some interesting lore and use their services on the island to your advantage.

As Kolkata choked on toxic air following Diwali and Kali Puja celebrations, West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari accused those raising concerns over firecracker pollution of being communists opposed to Hindu traditions. His remarks were consistent with the concerted push by a section of the Right wing to portray criticism of firecrackers as an attack on Hindu religious practices. However, among those complaining about noise levels and pollution in Kolkata were members of Adhikari’s own party and cabinet.
The Bengal CM made the remarks while addressing the media during a visit to the coastal town of Digha on Monday, where he had gone to attend an administrative meeting and visit the Kali Puja organised by the Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Traders Association.
Speaking to reporters, Adhikari said, “There has been an awakening of Sanatan in this state, and some people have a problem with that. The people making these allegations (about firecrackers) had turned Hindu religious festivals into cultural fests… These people do not apply ‘tika’ or religious markings on their foreheads, they do not wear ‘dors’ or religious threads on their wrists, nor do they wear tulsi beads around their necks.”
Adhikari further said, “The communists are raising this issue of firecrackers. We have controlled it in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directives. Firecrackers were burst in some places even after 10 pm, and the police took necessary action. We have stopped DJs, and we do not want environmental pollution. But people will have fun during Diwali. They will celebrate with lights and burst firecrackers. Where is the problem with that?”
While acknowledging that firecrackers had been burst beyond the time limit prescribed by the Supreme Court, Adhikari sought to deflect criticism by pointing to action taken by the administration.
“Those complaining that sound crackers were burst for a few hours longer than the time stipulated by the Supreme Court should know that the Pollution Control Board and the police are taking action against such violations. I would request those complaining about firecrackers to also congratulate the state government for stopping DJs. I will not say that DJ incidents did not happen in remote corners, but I did not hear them blaring, at least near the roads,” he said.
Firecrackers can Cure Diseases, Says Bengal Minister, then Apologises
According to the Supreme Court’s directives, only green firecrackers were allowed to be burst between 8 pm and 10 pm on Diwali. However, statements by ministers, the West Bengal Police’s deletion of a post urging responsible Diwali celebrations, and the general perception that a BJP government would not impose restrictions on Hindu festivals had collectively sent out a clear message: When it came to celebrating a majoritarian festival, the rules could be bent, if not ignored altogether.
BJP leader and Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikary said on Monday, “Our honourable chief minister has said that people will definitely burst firecrackers. How can we celebrate Kali Puja without firecrackers? But we will burst them in accordance with the instructions of the local police station. Also, many diseases can be prevented simply by lighting firecrackers.”
Although Adhikary later apologised and backtracked on her statement, claiming that the media had misinterpreted her remarks, the message had already got across.
A section of social media users also began targeting dissenting voices who tried to reason with their fellow citizens. A user named Partha Pratim Kundu, who describes himself as a wildlife photographer, asked in a post how elderlies, children and birds and animals survived in earlier times when there was no curb on firecrackers.
Another Facebook user, Chayan Mukherjee, who hailed the chief minister’s indulgence on firecrackers, claimed in a post that “most of the Indian environmentalists and human rights activists, as well as professors at various institutions, receive funding from outside to oppose the country’s development.”
Domkal’s CPI(M) MLA Mostafijur Rahaman Rana had urged people to celebrate Diwali as a festival of lights, without noise and loud firecrackers. BJP MLA Tarunjyoti Tiwari gave the issue a communal twist by asking whether the legislator would also call for a ‘bloodless Eid’.
State BJP leader Keya Ghosh also criticised Mostafijur Rahaman for advocating a noise-free and smoke-free Diwali.
The lone CPIM MLA of West Bengal had wished smokeless, soundless Diwali.

The political messaging was accompanied by widespread violations on the ground. A large section of the public openly flouted firecracker regulations. Almost all media outlets reported that loud firecrackers were burst throughout the night severely inconveniencing elderlies, children and also pets, birds and stray animals.
Kolkata’s AQI reached 623 around 11 pm on Sunday night, reported The telegraph. At 12.51 am on Monday, IQAir classified the city’s air quality as hazardous, recording an AQI of 532, with PM2.5 at 342 and PM10 at 405. Both particulate matter concentrations were several times higher than the WHO’s recommended limits.
Left with no other option, residents in several localities took matters into their own hands, protesting against the rampant bursting of firecrackers and intervening to stop it. Facebook user Anitesh Chakraborty narrated his experience in a post.
Chakraborty went up to a neighbouring apartment’s rooftop around 1.45 am to ask people bursting firecrackers to stop. While some residents supported his objection, others on nearby rooftops mocked him with gestures and taunts. Nevertheless, the intervention succeeded in stopping the firecrackers. He observed that the rooftops of apartment buildings had become spaces where people felt free to flout restrictions, and argued people to raise their voices against such violations.
According to a report by the Times of India, by 1 am, the West Bengal Pollution Control Board had received 84 noise-related complaints, while Kolkata Police had recorded 434 complaints.
Police rounded up 371 people for bursting illegal firecrackers, arresting 205 of them. Another 387 people were arrested for disorderly conduct. Several commentators pointed out that the most effective way to curb the use of illegal firecrackers was to stop their manufacture and sale. This year, only 238.6 kg of such products were seized, compared to 853 kg last year.
Kolkata’s high-rise buildings were particular hotspots for violations of firecracker and noise restrictions. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari himself acknowledged that the rules could not be enforced in every high-rise apartment building, as the state did not have enough police personnel.
Even hospitals located in silence zones were not spared. According to a report by The Telegraph, areas near hospitals such as B C Roy, R G Kar, M R Bangur and Sishumangal also faced onslaught of loud firecrackers.
To Celebrate Responsibly or Not? Bengal Police in a Fix
Signs of this situation had emerged earlier, when the West Bengal Police deleted a firecracker awareness post within hours of publishing it, as previously reported by Alt News.
Published on the morning of November 5 with the caption, “Please celebrate responsibly. It’s our Diwali too!”, the AI-generated poster featured two stray cats and a dog shivering due to the loud noise of firecrackers. However, it was deleted within three hours.
The post’s comment section was flooded with threatening messages directed at police and familiar Right-wing arguments, including questions about whether the police would also call for a ‘bloodless Eid’ and why the police and administration interfered only in Hindu festivals.
Similarly, Delhi Police, too, deleted a firecracker awareness post, while the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) removed a video featuring actor Dia Mirza advocating for a pollution-free Diwali from its social media accounts. Both decisions followed social media outrage from BJP-RSS supporters who claimed that the posts hurt Hindu religious sentiments.
A similar message by AISA leader Neha Bora also faced backlash from the far-right social media ecosystem.
It is that time of the year where our conversations will be accompanied by sore throats and respiratory problems.

BJP MLAs Complain about Noise Levels
Although a section of the Right wing encouraged unrestrained celebrations during Diwali and Kali Puja in the name of upholding Hindu traditions, some voices within the BJP struck a different note.
BJP leader and Sonarpur Dakshin MLA Roopa Ganguly tagged Kolkata Police in a post on Facebook stating she was unable to sleep because of the noise of firecrackers. However, the post is no longer available now.
State urban development minister Agnimitra Paul was seen roaming around the city in a police vehicle, attempting to curb the firecracker menace.
Paul said, “Please think about other people. Consider the condition of the elderly and the sick. The firecrackers are bursting so loudly that my heart is trembling.”
However, these interventions came too little, too late. The ruling dispensation had, through its rhetoric and its reluctance to enforce restrictions, effectively given people a free hand to flout the law, with the environment and public health bearing the consequences.
