The accident took place at around 2.30 pm, when the passenger vehicle, travelling from Bokakhat towards Nagaon, collided with the goods-carrying vehicle, officers said.
Islam, a resident of Golaghat who works for a construction company, was travelling in the bus with four of his co-workers. He said the vehicle, which had a capacity of hardly 30 passengers, was carrying at least 60 persons on Friday.
'Lucky to survive'
“I was sitting at the back, which is why I was lucky to survive. But the bus had too many passengers. Around 50% of them were standing, and even the cabin space, which was supposed to be free, was filled with passengers,” he said.
Also read | ‘Bus was overspeeding, violated restrictions’: Official on Assam accident that killed 26
Islam sustained a head injury in the collision but was discharged by doctors after receiving initial treatment.
Another passenger also alleged that the vehicle was overloaded and travelling at nearly 100 kmph. Recalling the moments before the collision, he said the bus suddenly lost control, crossed into the wrong lane and hit the oncoming truck.
“It was at high speed when it suddenly lost control, crossed into the wrong lane and hit the oncoming truck. I was sitting beside the window and saw it happen. I was so scared that I thought I would die,” he said.
The driver of the goods-carrying truck, who was also injured in the crash, offered a similar account of the collision, claiming that the bus suddenly entered his lane and rammed into the truck while he was driving on his proper side of the road.
Speaking to the media, the driver, whose identity has not yet been confirmed, said he was travelling from Tezpur when the bus approached from the opposite direction.
“I was coming this way from Tezpur and I was driving on the proper side. This bus suddenly came from the opposite direction. On such a wide road, it came directly into our lane and slammed straight into us, a direct head-on collision,” he said.
Describing the speed of the passenger vehicle, he added, “Yes, the bus hit us. It came at such a high speed, it's beyond words.” The driver said he sustained injuries to his hand and other parts of his body.
Dashcam footage emerges
The truck's dashcam footage, which has emerged following the accident, has captured the final moments before the collision.
The footage, authorised by the driver, could provide important clues about how the two vehicles approached each other immediately before the impact.
According to the doctors of the Jorhat Medical College and Hospital (JMCH), where the critical patients were shifted, said that around 12 injured persons are undergoing treatment.
The survivors' accounts have raised questions about the number of passengers travelling in the vehicle and whether overloading and speeding contributed to the crash.
Police said that they are investigating how many passengers were there in the bus and how many survivors are there.
Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi blamed alleged corruption, poor construction quality and a nexus between contractors and politicians for the tragedy, claiming it could have been avoided if highways were properly built and maintained.
Reacting to the accident, Gogoi alleged that national highways across Assam had become a “den of corruption” and questioned the government's collection of tolls despite the alleged poor condition of roads.
Assam Jatiya Parishad (AJP) president Lurinjyoti Gogoi urged the government to ensure advanced medical treatment for those critically injured and take responsibility for the families of those killed.
“Since Jorhat Medical College is there, the necessary medical care required for them must be provided. And for those who have died, the government will have to take responsibility for all their families,” he said.
He also called for stricter implementation of road safety measures and proper maintenance of national highways, saying that people's lives and futures depended on the condition of the roads.
Meanwhile, the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) and Asom Sena have offered to arrange blood donations for the injured.
AASU president Utpal Sarma said members of the organisation are ready to donate blood whenever required.

The first big sex scandal of the AI era has taken down Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and longtime CEO. Nvidia’s board of directors announced his resignation on Thursday morning and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
Jensen Huang is out. What now?
The former Nvidia CEO’s downfall is far bigger than one company.
Huang has been making headlines all week after news broke Friday that he had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singaporean tech firm Megaspeed who the US government alleges was also a Chinese spy.
The revelation Wednesday of a second extramarital affair, this time with an Nvidia employee reporting to Huang directly, added to the pressure, and another affair came to light later on Thursday after Huang’s ouster.
The scandal has implications far beyond one company: Huang’s central role in the AI race can’t be overstated. It was his vision of an AI future that led him to pivot Nvidia from a small company making video game chips into the dominant player in making the chips that serve OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google’s computing needs.
Huang is close friends with President Donald Trump’s and a leading voice in resisting efforts to slow AI progress. And he has pushed for the US to take a less hawkish position toward China’s own AI goals, a stance now called into question by his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Among its other impacts, the news has revived efforts on Capitol Hill to further restrict chip exports to China.
To break down the national security implications of Huang’s departure, how the Trump administration is involved, and what it says about US AI industry writ large, Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram spoke with Garret De Vynck, a technology reporter at the Washington Post.
Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get your podcasts, including Apple Podcasts, Pandora, and Spotify.
Nvidia has been called the central bank of AI, which is why it’s so important that we figure out what Jensen Huang may have disclosed to this alleged spy. How long has the president known about this, as far as we know?
As far as we know, the president has known about the fact that Jensen Huang was in a relationship with someone that the US government thought was a spy for about a year. This circulated within the administration, and the decision was made not to tell Jensen.
That doesn’t necessarily mean that it was automatically some kind of corrupt decision of President Trump protecting Jensen Huang. There’s all sorts of reasons why you might not want to tell someone they’re being spied on, the number one being that they might blow up the operation. Maybe you want to learn more. Maybe you suspect that the person themselves knows that they’re being spied on and is willingly sharing information and you need some more time to gather that. It’s unclear why the US government specifically chose not to pull in Jensen Huang.
It’s also a little bit unclear whether he knows he was being spied on, or whether maybe he was told through some kind of back channel. He has said that he did not know that she was a spy and he is admitting to the affair, to the infidelity. He’s admitting to essentially breaking Nvidia’s code of conduct by sleeping with one of its customers, but he is not admitting at all to knowing that she was a spy and definitely not admitting to sharing any information willfully.
It feels like this is the kind of thing that the government would investigate. There’s been reporting that the Commerce Department was involved with some kind of investigation, but that investigation came to an end and no one really knows why.
The context here is that the United States and China are in an AI race. Going back to the first Trump administration, there’s been pretty aggressive export controls saying, “We don’t want China to get our tech so that they can develop AI.” And the Biden administration continued that. He increased the export controls on China. China was complaining very loudly about this. They said, ‘We don’t care. We want to win AI and we need to slow you guys down.’
When Trump came in, he actually lifted his foot off the gas a little bit. They didn’t throw the gates open and say, “You can have whatever you want. All American companies can sell whatever they want to China.” But he said, “Some AI chips that are less powerful than the state of the art. We can send those to Chinese companies.“
The other thing that national security experts have pointed out is that the Trump administration could theoretically have been doing more to stop the smuggling of computer chips to China. And that’s where this story gets so important for national security.
Megaspeed is accused of essentially being a front for Chinese companies to get access to computer chips. Journalists have gone to Megaspeed’s office in Singapore where it’s based, and there were only a couple of people working there. It didn’t really seem like there was a lot going on. Nvidia has said all through this process over the last couple of years that, “No, we’ve checked it out, Megaspeed is a legitimate company and we’re not breaking the law when it comes to this.”
There are a lot of questions and what everyone is focused on finding out, both journalists and I would say congressional Democrats when they come into office in the new year is, is there something more going on here? Is there something where the Chinese either convinced Jensen Huang to sell more chips to them or Jensen Huang himself, who has been advocating for selling more chips to China, essentially did this himself?
“I think there’s this real question of: Do we see a much stronger push to actually ramp up controls on China and how does Trump respond?”
He’s been pressuring the president, he’s been donating to him, he’s been glad-handing with the president and the president has been listening more to this corporate executive who is his friend and who donated him a bunch of money rather than listening to China hawks or national security experts who say we should be limiting what China is able to access.
That’s really where the locus of this investigation is going to be. It’s not so much that Jensen Huang had an affair. It’s more the fact that he himself is someone who has said we need to sell more computer chips to China and he was involved with an alleged Chinese spy, and he’s very close to the president and had influence on the president.
You mentioned the Democrats. Have they said anything? Are they going to call him in front of Congress for an investigation?
Going forward, there are two big things here. One of them is these investigations into Jensen Huang and this whole situation. The company is likely going to continue to investigate. Maybe more information will come out there. Jensen Huang has been called to speak later this month in Congress. And congressional Democrats have also said that when they come into power in January, they will be asking him.
The second big thing that comes out of this is, what does America do when it comes to China and AI? Now that one of the biggest advocates for being a bit more friendly towards China when it comes to selling them things that they need for AI is out of the room and completely discredited, I think that the China hawks, those who say we need to crack down more aggressively, we need to limit China’s access to AI computer chips, they’re really coming into ascendance here and they’re in the Republican Party, they’re in the Democratic Party, some of them, people like Marco Rubio, are even in the Cabinet.
I think there’s this real question of: Do we see a much stronger push to actually ramp up controls on China and how does Trump respond? There’s all sorts of geopolitical things that could sort of spin out of this CEO affair.
I’m old enough to remember when a board tried to get rid of Sam Altman and then he was just back a week later. Elon Musk is already offering Jensen Huang a job. Is there a fair chance that he just goes somewhere that’s not that concerned about espionage affairs or getting with your VP of health or whatever it is? Is he just going to go work for China?
I don’t think he’s going to go work for China. This is definitely the wildest corporate story since Sam Altman was fired as CEO and brought back three or four days later. It’s a very different situation. That was a startup where you essentially have five or six investors who get to make the call about who the CEO is, and the employees at that company overwhelmingly wanted to bring Sam Altman back. I think they wanted more continuity of the company, but they also wanted to make sure that their company didn’t go under and go bankrupt and get disappeared, which was sort of on the table at that point in time.
Nvidia’s not going anywhere. Obviously employees have lost a lot of money in terms of the stock value already coming down due to the situation. So employees are probably shocked. They’re probably upset. Jensen Huang is broadly loved at Nvidia, and so I can definitely see that employees would be doing petitions, asking for him to return.
But this is a giant public company and the board makes a decision here. Jensen Huang was untruthful publicly and I think that also will make other public companies hesitant before rushing to bring him on as CEO.
As we’ve talked about many times in the show, half of our economy is staked on AI at this point. How concerned should we be that one of the most important people in this industry was so easily duped in this honeypot situation? Are these the people we should be trusting with the future of our society?
It’s a really good reminder that people are people. I think that we like to lionize individuals and say that they are the ones who are going to take us into the future and they are inventing the future and it’s so incredible. And I do think Jensen Huang gets a lot of credit for making sure that the companies kept up in AI, but at the end of the day, it was also a lucky break for them that the computer chips they were making just happened to work well for the math that is required by artificial intelligence.
I do think that this speaks to something that a lot of people across the country and maybe even the world really feel. They do not want to sign off the future to a dozen dudes in Silicon Valley and their collaborators in the Trump White House. I think that is a view that a lot of people increasingly have. I think it was one of the factors in the midterms, maybe not the most important one, but people are concerned about concentration of power. They’re concerned about AI and they don’t see it as something that they themselves have control over.
I think that this is just going to be another thing that sort of adds skepticism to the idea that people like Jensen Huang should be the ones making the final decision when it comes to artificial intelligence.

In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that all men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.
Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.
The new guidance departs from ACS’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. The recommendation was similar to that from the US Preventive Services Task Force, a federal panel that regularly evaluates evidence and makes recommendations on such preventive medical care. (The USPSTF is currently working on an update to its prostate cancer screening recommendation, though it should be noted that the panel has recently been overhauled by anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and new members are reportedly rife with conflicts of interest.)

Over two years after 
Sheikh Hasina
 fled to India, New Delhi is reportedly looking to send the former Bangladesh prime minister back to Dhaka, but has laid down two conditions for Tarique Rahman's government.
According to a BBC Bangla report, India wants Bangladesh to send a military aircraft to bring Hasina back from New Delhi. However, the proposal comes with conditions, as Hasina has been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court over her government's crackdown on protesters during the July 2024 uprising.
The first condition is that the Bangladesh army must take responsibility for bringing its longest-serving leader Hasina back, preferably using a military aircraft. This would mirror her arrival in India aboard a Bangladesh military aircraft after she fled the country on August 5, 2024.
The second condition is that Bangladesh must guarantee Hasina an opportunity to appeal her death sentence and face a fresh trial over allegations linked to the July 2024 killings.
Why does India want Sheikh Hasina back in Bangladesh
The BBC Bangla report said Hasina's continued stay in India has increasingly become an uncomfortable issue for the government, affecting its bilateral ties with Bangladesh and attracting international criticism.
India has faced criticism for sheltering a former leader convicted by a Bangladeshi court in connection with the deadly crackdown on protesters, the report said.
More than two years after Hasina sought refuge in India following the mass uprising in July 2024, New Delhi is increasingly looking for a way to resolve the sensitive issue with its neighbouring country.
India's preferred option would have been for Hasina to move to a third country. However, repeated efforts by New Delhi to explore this possibility with different countries failed for various reasons, according to the report.
What has Sheikh Hasina said about returning to Bangladesh
Hasina has maintained that she intends to return to Bangladesh, previously telling news agency Reuters in an interview that she planned to go back in December 2026.
However, she has not announced a specific date.
The former prime minister has also acknowledged the risks involved in returning, including the possibility of arrest, imprisonment or even an attempt on her life.
"Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me. I have considered all these possibilities. But, you know, I stopped worrying about my personal safety a long time ago. I returned to Bangladesh in 1981, despite military rule. I returned again in 2007, knowing that the military-backed government might arrest me. I have faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on my life.
 Fear has never stopped me from doing what I believe is right," the exiled leader said in an audio statement.
In an interview with news agency IANS, Hasina also expressed concern over the situation in Bangladesh. She alleged that Awami League leaders and workers were being persecuted, while ordinary people were suffering, losing their homes and livelihoods.
She described the country as going through a difficult phase, raising concerns over the treatment of political supporters and the broader situation under the new Dhaka government led by Tarique Rahman.

SpaceX to attempt double catch of huge Starship rocket
- Published
SpaceX will attempt to catch both parts of its huge Starship rocket after it launches on its next test flight on Friday.
Elon Musk's company will use the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower to grab the rocket parts mid-air as they return to Earth.
If successful, this will be the first full recovery of a rocket that's been to space, paving the way for making Starship reusable so it can fly repeatedly.
Nasa will be closely watching the flight: the SpaceX rocket is set to play a vital part in its Artemis programme, which will see astronauts land on the Moon.
The 124m-tall rocket is scheduled to blast off from the Starbase launchpad in Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) with a 75-minute-long launch window.
After six and a half minutes, the first planned catch will be attempted when the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - returns to the launch tower.
The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, will continue its journey to space and deploy 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high speed internet from space.
The Ship is then due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning for the second catch attempt about 22 and a half hours after taking off.
Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights.
But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean.
SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space.
If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean.
Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX.
In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster.
Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than a hundred times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch.
But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, President of Royal Aeronautical Society.
"A successful double catch would be visually spectacular, but full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said.
"One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate."
- What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? 
  - Published27 October
- Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test 
  - Published28 September
After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency.
The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline.
SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface.
But it's not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down.
Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule.
This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers.
Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended.
But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida.
Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027.
Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

Washington, Nov 14: The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon for just the second time since the September 11 attacks, with officials citing “extraordinary circumstances" caused by communications problems at regional air traffic control centres.
The nation's top homeland security official attributed the problem to a telecommunications outage and said there was no indication yet of a nefarious act. But the consequences were profound, disrupting potentially thousands of planned flights through at least late Friday night and upending travel plans for passengers who were heading home, expected as wedding guests or had other weekend plans.
“It's frustrating. This certainly sounds like it's going to be more than the usual run-of-the-mill delay. I look forward to finding out why,” said Jeff Dubner, a Washington, DC, attorney, whose Alaska Airlines flight from Los Angeles to Washington, DC, was already half an hour late and taxiing to the runway when the plane came to a halt.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Friday's restrictions were imposed “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," according to an FAA notice. The agency was investigating a communication issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centres that direct planes en route between airports nationwide, said Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
A few international flights were taking off Friday evening from international aviation hubs on the East and West coasts.
Top official says no sign yet of nefarious act
----------------------------------------------
Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that there was no indication yet that “this was a nefarious attack against us. It's just a telecommunications outage as of right now.”
“Everybody's safe. There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying,” Mullin said.
At least 600 flights have been diverted so far as a result of the FAA's order to ground all air traffic nationwide.
As of 5:50 pm Eastern, 496 flights were diverted to the airport from where they originally took off, while 104 were sent to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.
Among the airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted are Chicago O'Hare International Airport, Denver International Airport, Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.
Some 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers were scheduled to take off from airports in the US after 4 p.m. Eastern, raising the likelihood of more cancellations and flight diversions.
At Chicago O'Hare Airport on Friday afternoon, travellers passing through security learned about the ground stop when they gazed up at screens that showed flight delays across the board.
Some called friends or family members, debating whether to stay the night in Chicago or find another way to their destinations.
Amber McQuilkin, 27, sat on a bench, disappointed that she might miss a trip with friends to New York for the League of Legends world finals. Her friends, she said, had already arrived there.
“There's not really any information being passed to me,” said the Seattle software engineer, who took a week of vacation for the trip. “I contemplated just abandoning the flight and driving, but then the more I thought about it, the more I'm like, that would be miserable.”
Austin Curtis and his wife were rethinking their trip from South Bend, Indiana, to a friend's baby shower in Denver after getting delayed during a layover in Chicago.
They had boarded a flight to Denver from O'Hare International Airport when they were told to get off the plane.
“We did see them taking luggage off our plane and others, so we're assuming it's going to be a pretty substantial delay,” Curtis said.
They were unsure whether to get a hotel room or keep waiting out the delay at the airport. With care already in place for their two young children at home, they might stay the weekend in Chicago, he said.
“We might just make the most of it,” Curtis said.
Despite the nationwide FAA ground stop, SpaceX launched its Starship rocket from Texas on Friday afternoon on its latest test flight.
The government has been working to overhaul outdated technology
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
There is no timeline for restarting flights. Mullin said investigators will look at whether there is any link to the FAA's nationwide rollout of a new artificial intelligence system to help identify problems and reroute planes.
But that system operates out of one location near Washington, DC, and just sends recommendations to the air traffic control centres.
The government has been working to overhaul the outdated technology that air traffic controllers rely on since Congress approved USD 12.5 billion for the project last year. Miles of old copper wires have been replaced with fibre optic lines and old radio systems are gradually being replaced at airports across the country.
But much work remains. Duffy has said that another USD 30 billion will be needed to complete the work, and the White House has begun lobbying Congress to approve it.
The problem appeared similar to a regional air traffic control communication outage in September that snarled hundreds of flights across the Northeast, aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said, except this time on a nationwide scale. It may be linked to the outdated technology used by air traffic controllers.
“If you don't have that ability, whether it's because the old wires that they have are just run down or for whatever reason, you've got to stop airplanes on the ground,” said Arroyo, who is a former United Airlines pilot. “And not put them in the air where you're going to risk not being able to communicate with them.”
Friday's ground stop was different from the one after September 11 because planes were not being told to land immediately and pilots likely were able to communicate with ground controllers at airports, Arroyo said.

Quick Answer
You can edit Instagram Reels on Mac using Claude AI and the free Instagram Edits app. Install Claude Code, enable the app’s MCP automation server, and connect both. Then use simple text prompts to create projects, arrange clips, add transitions, titles, and effects, and export finished Reels in 4K.
The wait is over. The Instagram Edits app is finally available on desktop, but only on macOS, as of this guide. Instagram Edits is my go-to app not just for editing Instagram Reels, but also a reliable free video editor with all the features and a simple design.
Although the app is designed for creators and competes with CapCut, it has been limited to Android and iOS so far. But a few months ago, Instagram announced a desktop version, and now it is finally here. Right now, the app is only available on macOS, with Windows and other platforms coming in future releases.
I have been using the app for the past couple of days. It is very similar to the mobile app and is also free to use, but it also features an MCP connection, which you can use to connect to any of your AI subscriptions, such as Claude, Codex, and Muse, and let AI edit your videos.
The desktop interface is slightly different and can be complex for beginners. It took me a while to get used to it, but I have created a detailed guide to get started.
I also created a guide on how to connect your MCP, like Claude, to Instagram Edits to edit your videos, and it covers everything about this feature, including common setup errors. This guide is for beginners, so each step is comprehensive and detailed.
Table of Contents
How to Connect Claude AI to Instagram Edits and Edit Reels on Mac
Before connecting your Instagram Edits app to the MCP server, ensure you have the following pre-requirements:
- A Mac with an Apple chip (M1 or newer) on macOS 15.1 or later. Currently, the Instagram Edits desktop app is only available for macOS, with Windows and Linux versions coming soon, but there is no expected release date yet.
- Download and install the Instagram Edits app from here
- A paid AI subscription for any model; you can also use the free AI model.
Part 1: Get Claude Code
Step 1: Open Terminal and type the command: claude –version, and press Return. If you see a version number, it means Claude Code is already installed on your device. You can skip to Part 2 to continue setup.
If you see something like zsh: command not found: claude, it means Claude Code is not installed on your device, or Terminal can not find it yet. Follow the next steps to install Claude Code on your Mac.
Install Claude Code: To install Claude Code, use the official Anthropic installer. To do that, open Terminal on your Mac and paste this command: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
Wait a few minutes, and then you will see a ” Claude Code successfully installed message in your terminal.
Check the setup notes below. If you see something like installation exists but ~/.local/bin is not in your PATH, it means the terminal still can’t find Claude Code yet.
Now follow the next two steps. If you don’t see such a note, you can quit the terminal, reopen it, and use this command to confirm that Claude Code has been successfully installed on your device: confirm claude –version. If you see a Claude version, it’s installed on your device. Then continue with part two.
Next, paste this command into the terminal and press Enter: echo ‘export PATH=”$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH”‘ >> ~/.zshrc
Next, paste this: source ~/.zshrc, and press Enter. Now type claude –version and press Enter. You will see the Claude version number. This means Claude Code is successfully installed on your device in the terminal
Part 2: Turn on Claude access in Edits
Next, you need to let Claude access your Instagram edits apps. First, ensure the Instagram edits app is installed on your Mac. If not, you can use the official download link here. Once installed, follow the steps below:
Step 1: Open the app on your Mac and sign in with your account. On the home screen, you will go directly to the Projects tab.
Step 2: Next, you can tap on your profile picture in the top right corner of the screen or click on the edit option in the menu bar at the top of the screen and then click on the settings
Step 3: Next, tap on the automation from the sidebar
Step 4: By default, automation is turned off. Now, from the automation settings, turn on the toggle that says Enable Automation Server.
Step 5: Under the Connect an AI Client section, click the copy icon next to the Claude code. This will copy the connection command with your access token. Remember, don’t share this command with others. In this case, I am using Claude code. If you are using Codex, tap the copy button next to Codex. The same goes for Muse.
You can also connect any AI model. Since it is a standard MCP server, any AI app can connect to the MCP server over HTTPS and can control edits.
Remember to replace <TOKEN> with the Access token from Edits > Settings > Automation, and keep Edits open with the automation server turned on
For Google Gemini CLI:
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For Qwen:
npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code
qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp
For DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM, and most others, we can use OpenCode
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash
{
“$schema”: “https://opencode.ai/config.json”,
“mcp”: {
“servers”: {
“edits”: {
“type”: “remote”,
“url”: “http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp”,
“oauth”: false,
“headers”: { “Authorization”: “Bearer <TOKEN>” }
}
}
}
}
Part 3: Connect Claude Code to Edits
Next, let’s connect Claude Code (or any AI model) to edits. Remember that you can only do this once.
Step 1: Now, paste the command you copied from the previous section into the terminal. You will see: Added HTTP MCP server metapilot-native
Step 2: Next, for Claude, paste this command: claude mcp get metapilot-native and press Enter. Under status, if you see Connected, it worked. If it says Failed to connect, ensure the edits app is running and follow the previous steps carefully.
For other models, follow these:
| App (models) | Connect command | Check it worked | 
| Claude Code (Claude) | claude mcp add –transport http –scope user metapilot-native http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” | claude mcp get metapilot-native | 
| Gemini CLI (Gemini) | gemini mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | gemini mcp list | 
| Qwen Code (Qwen) | qwen mcp add –transport http –scope user –header “Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>” edits http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp | qwen mcp list | 
| Codex (OpenAI GPT) | echo ‘export EDITS_TOKEN=”<TOKEN>”‘ >> ~/.zshrc && source ~/.zshrc && codex mcp add edits –url http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp –bearer-token-env-var EDITS_TOKEN | Run codex, then type /mcp | 
| OpenCode (DeepSeek, Grok, Mistral, Kimi, GLM and more) | No command. Paste the opencode.jsonc block from my last message into the folder you run OpenCode in. | opencode mcp list | 
| LM Studio (local Llama, Gemma, Qwen, DeepSeek R1) | No command. Program tab, then Install, then Edit mcp.json, and paste the JSON block. | Look at the Program tab | 
| Cursor (any model it offers) | No command. Paste the same JSON into ~/.cursor/mcp.json. | Cursor Settings, then MCP | 
Part 4: Start Claude Code
Now go to the folder where the videos are saved to edit them using Instagram edits. I recommend that you store all the videos in the Movies folder so it is easy to access in the future. In this case, I stored all my files in the Movies folder on my Mac. Now, once you have access to the folder, follow the steps below.
Step 1: To use Claude, go to the folder using the CD command. For example: cd ~/Downloads or cd ~/Movies. In my case, cd ~/Movies. Next, once you are in the folder, Type Cluade and press Return.
Step 2: Claude will ask whether you trust the folder you provided. Use the down arrow and select I trust this folder, and press Enter. It asks only once, and once you give permission, you can store all future videos in this folder for edits.
Step 3: To check, you can type /mcp and press Enter. It lists the apps Claude Code is connected to. metapilot-native with a green tick means Claude can control Edits.
Step 4: Go to the metapilot-native option and press Enter to see more details. You can use the down or up arrow to navigate between the options.
Part 5: Make your first Reel with Claude
Now let’s use Claude to create my first reel. In this case, I asked Claude to edit a 50-second coffee reel from five clips. In your case, you can store all the clips in the folder. First, test the connection again. Once done, follow the steps below.
To test the connection, go to your folder and type list my Instagram edits projects and press Enter. You will see metabolist native and the table of all your edit projects.
Step 2 : Now you can ask Claude to make edits for the Instagram reel video. You can manually create a new project, add clips, and point Claude to the project title and edit your videos, or you can ask Claude to create a project, add clips, and edit your first reel. I recommend giving Claude the full location of your clips and the title.
Step 3: That’s it. Claude will now create a new project and add Sunclips. You can open the Instagram Edits app to see the changes.
Step 4: Once you’ve loaded the clips, you can ask Claude to add transitions between them and also add titles, sound effects, and much more. In this case, I’m asking Claude to add the title “Morning Coffee” in big white text for two seconds and then add smooth transitions between the clips.
Step 5: Once you’ve made the edits, you can also ask Claude Core to export the clips in 4K, and it does it for you.
Step 6: Once the video is exported, Claude notifies you of the length, format, and size. You can open the same folder to see the clip. Claude also notifies you where the clip is stored and its title.

How do you think you’re going to die?
If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US, it’s reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week, Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, “I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident.”
In the opening lecture of a three-part series, Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending “AI takeover.” He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems “call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth” and where any human trying to stop them “would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military.” Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.
Despite his grim assessment of our collective mortality risk, Cristiano admitted in his talk that there’s no “quantitative model” that can “put a number” on the likelihood of this kind of AI takeover. In almost the same breath, though, he said that if AI continues to develop at “the most rapid trajectory,” humanity is “looking at something like a coin flip of an AI takeover,” including a “meaningful risk” of one happening in the next six to 12 months. And even with realistic policy responses slowing things down, the risk remains “exceptionally high,” he said.
From here to there
Unlike some other recent AI doomsday prognosticators who have been a bit vague about the “how” of it all, Cristiano used his lecture to spin a step-by-step tale of escalating AI threats that sounds like it could come from a science-fiction novel. That line of reasoning leans heavily on this summer’s OpenAI/Hugging Face hacking incident as an example of “roughly the things we might expect to see shortly before something really bad were to happen.”

Drone and missile strikes have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East this year, disrupting cloud services for millions of people and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This trend represents a new concern for Big Tech companies—but also for governments and everyone else who depends on common digital services in modern life.
To explore what this all means for modern society’s reliance on cloud resilience, I will be hosting a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET with Joseph Jarnecki, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), a UK defense and security think tank. He leads RUSI’s work on how cloud services factor into national security and defense, along with tech sovereignty efforts.
Jarnecki has done extensive research on how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite facing both cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of the full-scale Russian invasion, and explored what that means for NATO and European governments’ cloud adoption plans.
This year, Jarnecki has written about Iran’s drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran, and the broader implications for governments and Big Tech. He has also commented on the impacts of Russia and Ukraine exchanging strikes on each other’s data centers.

Scientists have assembled a cellular atlas of a crucial brain region called the basal ganglia involved in functions such as movement, decision making, emotions and habit formation — an accomplishment that could help guide new treatments for several devastating diseases.
The researchers mapped the cell types and cellular gene activity in the basal ganglia, an interconnected set of structures deep within the brain, in humans as well as in mice and in macaque and marmoset monkeys. Basal ganglia dysfunction is associated with conditions such as Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease, schizophrenia, Tourette’s syndrome, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder and addiction.
“It is important to understand the structure and function of the basal ganglia in order to develop effective treatments of these diseases,” said neuroscientist Hongkui Zeng, director of brain science at the Allen Institute in Seattle and one of the leaders of the research presented in more than two dozen studies published on Thursday in Cell and related journals.
“It is a major milestone in our journey toward a comprehensive, detailed, multimodal, cross-species aligned cell atlas for the entire human brain,” with a target date sometime in 2028, Zeng added.
The research was conducted as part of the BRAIN Initiative, an effort launched in 2014 to advance the understanding of the brain with the support of the US National Institutes of Health. The work presented on Thursday offers the first comprehensive cross-species cellular roadmap for any brain region.
“Until now, there was no reference describing each cell type in the human basal ganglia together with how it regulates its genes,” said Joseph Ecker, a molecular biologist and geneticist at the Salk Institute in La Jolla, California, another of the research leaders.
“In the near term, the atlas is a reference resource for researchers. We are studying a Parkinson’s gene and can now see which cell types turn that gene on, and which DNA switches are active in those cells. Over the longer term, the atlas can help identify cell-type-specific targets for gene therapy and gene editing,” Ecker said. “It also gives a baseline for comparing diseased tissue with healthy tissue.”
Therapies built on the new work are still years away, Ecker said.
Among other findings, researchers identified a new type of brain cell associated with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, documented genetic changes in specific cell types that could play a role in autism, and discovered changes in gene activity in certain cells associated with aging.
Cross-species comparisons
Using brain tissue from deceased human donors, the researchers examined the role of 21 million cells in the basal ganglia in people, as well as millions more cells in the three other species.
“Understanding the cellular composition of this brain structure across species will allow for comparative analyses of function as well as connectivity patterns and response to pharmacological interventions,” said Salk Institute neuroscientist and biochemist Margarita Behrens, another of the research leaders.
Many studies for ethical reasons cannot be performed using living human brains. Much of what was previously known about the basal ganglia, and most early testing of new treatments, had come from research involving mice and monkeys.
“We rely on animal models to probe the inner workings of brain cells and circuits in generating brain function and mediating disease effects, and to test the efficacies of therapeutic interventions,” Zeng said.
The structures of the basal ganglia include the striatum, globus pallidus and substantia nigra.
“Together they help select and start movements, and they support habit formation, reward learning, motivation and emotion,” Ecker said.
The atlas combines several layers of data. One shows which genes are switched on in each cell. Another involves the epigenome, a collection of chemical compounds and proteins that attach to the DNA and regulate gene activity. A third layer involves spatial maps showing where each cell type sits in the tissue of the basal ganglia.
“Most of the DNA variants linked to brain disorders lie outside the protein-coding parts of genes. Many of them sit in DNA ‘switches’ that control when and where genes turn on, and those switches are often active only in particular cell types,” Ecker said.
The protein-coding parts of genes carry genetic instructions used to build proteins, the complex molecules that perform most of the critical work inside cells.
An atlas like this one helps trace a disease-risk DNA variant to the specific kind of nerve cell or support cell where it acts.
“That is a first step toward understanding how the variant contributes to disease, and eventually toward treating it,” Ecker said.

Outage at HR platform Workday locks millions of employees out of their account
The company placed its system in maintenance mode after discovering an issue.
A widespread Workday outage on the evening of November 13 left employees unable to clock in and out, access their pay info, request for time off or file for benefits. According to San Francisco Chronicle, the human resources platform said it placed some of its systems into maintenance mode to fix an issue it discovered during testing. Specifically, the problem left some information inconsistent, and the company said it could cause errors when users try to access their accounts or complete tasks within its system. There was a spike in reports at Downdetector at around 5:19PM Eastern time, though it has tapered off since then.

The company has apologized for the disruption and said that it's looking for the best way to fix the problem.

As telescopes go, few if any are more famous than the Hubble Space Telescope. Over 30 years of operations, the telescope has been essential to groundbreaking discoveries that have fundamentally transformed humanity’s view of the universe. But like all satellites in low Earth orbit, it’s been gradually descending.
This happens because of atmospheric drag, and the Hubble Space Telescope is not equipped with a propulsion system to adjust its own orbit. According to NASA’s analysis, if left unchecked, the telescope will likely re-enter Earth’s atmosphere in 2033 or 2034, eventually crashing back onto the planet.
Hoping to delay this conclusion, NASA has issued a formal Request for Information seeking proposals from the private sector for “in-space servicing” of the famous telescope. This would likely involve raising Hubble’s altitude to extend its operational lifespan, but the agency is also open to industry’s suggestions for managing a safe and controlled reentry or disposal of the telescope while still in orbit. Space companies can also propose upgrades to enhance the telescope’s functionality in its remaining years.
“Hubble is a national icon,” Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, said in a statement. “Given the time we have until Hubble’s anticipated reentry, we are eager to explore the breadth of possibilities to boost Hubble to a higher orbit while we develop the flagship mission to follow.”
The telescope was designed with the expectation that astronauts would perform repairs and upgrades in orbit. Since it was launched in 1990, a total of five service missions have been carried out. The last of these missions was canceled after the space shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003. But NASA later determined that the benefits of servicing Hubble outweighed the risks of a final mission, and in 2009 a crew took measures, such as replacing the battery, to extend the telescope’s lifespan.
This is also not the first time NASA has considered private-sector resources for raising the Hubble Space Telescope’s orbit. In September 2022, NASA entered into a nonfunding partnership agreement with SpaceX to investigate the possibility of using the company’s Dragon spacecraft to move Hubble into a more stable orbit. However, according to NASA’s announcement at the time, the agency had no plans to conduct or fund the service mission itself; the study was intended solely to assess commercial feasibility.
Meanwhile, NASA commissioned the private company Katalyst Space Technologies in September 2025 to perform an orbital raise for the Swift Observatory, which was experiencing faster-than-expected orbital decay. However, the company’s spacecraft, launched in July 2026, suffered an attitude control malfunction, forcing the mission to be abandoned. On November 4, Swift reentered the atmosphere over Indonesia.
The problems facing the Hubble Space Telescope are not limited to its drop in altitude. The spacecraft itself is also experiencing malfunctions. In June 2024, NASA announced that it would transition the Hubble Space Telescope to a new operating mode using only one of the six gyros on board to assess the telescope’s orientation. After more than three decades in space, only three of the gyros were operational, and one of those was starting to return abnormal readings. The other remaining functional gyro is now being kept in a ready state for future use.
NASA estimates that a mission to raise the telescope’s orbit will need to be carried out by 2032. In an announcement made in 2022, NASA also explained that if the Hubble Space Telescope could be raised to a higher, more stable orbit, it could continue to observe the cosmos for several more years.
“Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible,” said NASA administrator Jared Isaacman. “If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already in orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble’s life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe.”

Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen’s purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google’s ecosystem use.
With Google’s recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company’s products.
Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon.

Online travel aggregator (OTA) Yatra swung to the red and reported a consolidated net loss of ₹78.4 Lakhs in the second quarter (Q2) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27). In contrast, the travel tech platform has reported a net profit of ₹14.3 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹33.9 Lakhs in Q1 FY27. The losses came despite the company raking in ₹1.7 Cr in one-time deferred tax benefits during the quarter. The bottom line was primarily impacted as the company’s revenue from operations tanked 39.1% to ₹213.6 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹350.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, on a sequential basis, Yatra’s top line rose 13.7% from ₹187.9 Cr in the preceding quarter. The OTA attributed the losses to the “challenging operating environment”, lower MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions) volumes, and the reorientation of the MICE vertical towards smaller corporate group programmes. “... Our year-on-year profitability was impacted primarily by MICE, which faced an exceptionally strong comparable quarter last year and a tactical shift towards smaller corporate group programmes amid prevailing uncertainty…,” said Yatra CEO Siddhartha Gupta. Including other income of ₹4.4 Cr, Yatra’s total income stood at ₹218 Cr in Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter under review declined 35% to ₹219.9 Cr compared to ₹339 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also incurred an additional tax expense of ₹59.3 Lakh during the quarter. Revenue less service cost (RLSC), which is essentially the gross margin, declined 0.2% to ₹125.5 Cr in Q2 FY27. As a result, EBITDA declined 47% YoY to ₹13.2 Cr, while EBITDA margin stood at 10.48%during the quarter under review. In a statement, the company’s gross bookings grew 6% YoY and 3% QoQ to ₹2,165.5 Cr in Q2 FY27. During the quarter, Yatra said that it added 54 new corporate customers with an estimated annual revenue potential of ₹203.5 Cr. “We continue to make progress on our strategic priorities, including expanding into the SME and mid-market segments through Travel Pro, strengthening our expense management offering through RECAP, expanding hotel supply and leveraging AI-led automation. These initiatives are helping us broaden our addressable market and build a more scalable business, positioning us for sustainable growth and improved profitability over the medium term,” added Gupta. Yatra’s US Entity On Nasdaq’s Radar Separately, the travel tech platform’s US-listed entity, Yatra Online Inc, said that it has received a letter from Nasdaq after its shares traded below the exchange’s minimum $1 closing bid price for more than a month. This has effectively put the travel tech company on a compliance watch. The company said that the notice does not immediately delist the company’s shares from the Nasdaq Capital Market. However, the OTA said that it has been given a timeline of 180 days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance. To do so, its shares must close at $1 or higher for at least 10 consecutive business days, even though Nasdaq may require up to 20 consecutive days in certain cases. If Yatra fails to meet the requirement by May next year, it may qualify for an additional 180-day compliance period. This would require the company to meet Nasdaq’s other continued-listing thresholds and formally notify the exchange of its intention to cure the deficiency. A reverse stock split is among the options available to lift the share price. Yatra said it may consider such a move if necessary, but cautioned that there is no assurance it will regain compliance. Nevertheless, Yatra said it intends to closely monitor its closing bid price and may evaluate available options to restore compliance. The notice highlights the pressure facing the travel-tech company’s US-listed shares. As of 1:13 AM IST, shares of Yatra Online Inc were trading at $0.77, down 18% in the past six months and nearly 57% lower on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. This comes as the US-listed Yatra Online Inc has been reporting increased net losses, compressed margins and falling revenues. Slowing growth in core verticals, market volatility and rising short-term trade-related borrowings have further led to the sell-off in the stock. But a sustained share price below $1 can further reduce liquidity, deter institutional investors and complicate future fundraising. Meanwhile, shares of India-listed Yatra closed Thursday’s trading session 0.94% lower at ₹81.03 on the BSE.

Review the listed files carefully, uncheck the ones you don’t want to delete, and click the Delete selected button to get rid of them. Be sure to back up your registry if you’ll be deleting leftover registry keys.
When you uninstall apps this way, you’ll need to click through multiple dialog box menus to complete the uninstallation. You can save yourself this hassle by clicking the Quiet Uninstall button instead of Uninstall after selecting apps for deletion. Bulk Crap Uninstaller will try — wherever possible — to uninstall apps silently. You won’t see visual confirmation in this mode.
Other Bulk Crap Uninstaller Features You Should Know About
For most people, the standard uninstallation process we checked out above is enough to get the job done. However, Bulk Crap Uninstaller has a few advanced features that can help you get the most out of the app.
For example, Bulk Crap Uninstaller offers a CLI version called BCU-console. It’s a great option for those who want to clean up their PC without dealing with multiple windows. Similarly, it lets you run an uninstallation script with your selected apps to automate deletion. This can be useful for cleaning up new PCs, too. Just feed the app a list of all the pre-installed apps from Windows, and it will remove them. You can go through Bulk Crap Uninstaller’s documentation to learn more about using scripts.
Bulk Crap Uninstaller can also run portably. So, you can put it on a USB flash drive and run it directly. This is handy when you want to uninstall apps on a PC running very low on storage space or one that isn’t connected to the internet and can’t download the Bulk Crap Uninstaller app.
Last but not least, Bulk Crap Uninstaller is highly configurable. As such, you can configure its behavior per your preference. Click the gear icon in the top toolbar to access the app’s settings. Here, you can change things like where to look for apps, which items to show/omit, and how the list appears. You can also configure the default behavior of quiet uninstallation and how many concurrent uninstalls the app can perform, among other things.
What I’m Not a Fan Of
I’ve used Bulk Crap Uninstaller on my PC for a while, and although it does its job well, there are a few aspects that I’m not a fan of and wish were better. The biggest one is that the app’s interface can seem intimidating, especially to first-time users. In other words, it looks more like a developer tool than a regular consumer app. It’s best to spend some time exploring different menus and options the app offers before jumping straight into uninstalling apps.
Then, there’s the risk of over-cleaning. Because Bulk Crap Uninstaller can scan deep system components, too, it’s important to double-check the selection — and not blindly trust the populated list — before uninstallation. You can configure the settings to minimize the risk. Another thing I’ve noticed is that the quiet uninstallation mode sometimes doesn’t work: some apps don’t obey it and keep popping up dialog boxes that require confirmation before uninstallation. Although rare, some users have complained about aggressive registry scanning, wherein Bulk Crap Uninstaller highlights shared keys (those used by other apps too) for removal. You can avoid this by reviewing the registry keys highlighted for deletion.
These aren’t drawbacks of Bulk Crap Uninstaller, though; they’re just a trade-off for its advanced capabilities. For this reason, it’s important to configure the app before you start using it and be completely sure about the actions you perform using it. You should also create a Restore Point when dealing with apps with broken uninstallers or stubborn leftovers. This way, if the cleanup goes wrong and renders your PC unusable, you can roll back to the last working state and undo the action.

How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
"We need new leadership," says Senator Chris Van Hollen, who on Thursday announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Democratic majority leader. Van Hollen has garnered support among Democrats for his sharp criticism of the Trump administration, including their upheaval of U.S. programs to promote health and end poverty around the world.
In an interview with NPR on Tuesday, two days before his announcement, Van Hollen spoke to NPR about his plans to "shine a light on all the harm and damage the Trump administration's done to our country and our interests around the world" — and what the Democrats hope to accomplish with foreign aid.
As the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee, which oversees the State Department and what's left of the United States Agency for International Development, he could have considerable sway over how Congress investigates and legislates on foreign aid.
This interview has been edited for clarity and length. NPR reached out to the State Department for comment but did not receive a response in time for publication.
You've taken a strong stand against the Trump administration's shakeup of foreign aid. You led protests against the dissolution of USAID and in a hearing last year told Secretary of State Marco Rubio that "People died because of those actions, mothers, fathers and children." You've also authored statements condemning a range of actions, including tying health aid to mineral deals. In the majority, what's the first step you'd take on the aid front?
Priority number one is to do an analysis of all the harm the Trump administration has done.
There have been very credible analyses showing that over 700,000 people around the world died between January 2025 and January 2026 because of cuts to USAID. If these trends continue, you're talking about millions of people dying in the coming years.
One of the great benefits of being in the majority, is you actually have a gavel and can call a public hearing, and use that as a spotlight to help educate people around the country.
We can do that to show the consequences of Elon Musk taking a chainsaw to USAID. I remember to this day a scene at the White House [in February 2025] when Donald Trump was at his desk and Elon Musk was standing behind him, and a reporter asked Elon Musk about the cuts to fighting Ebola, and Elon Musk's response was essentially, "Whoops, yeah, we missed that." And then he claimed that they'd restored it. Well, we know that they've not restored it adequately — there's good evidence that the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo could have been better contained if the United States had not made big cuts to public health.
We can investigate what they did, not for the purpose of putting it back exactly as it was but understanding the damage that has been done, fully, with an eye toward reforming it.
You've already been speaking out against a lot of this in the minority. What kinds of actions can Democrats take as a majority that they couldn't before?
Being in the majority makes a big difference. Now we have many more tools available, specifically through the power of the purse.
One of the things the Trump administration has done is essentially sit on funds appropriated by the Congress for public health here at home but also for international health programs. So there's an example where we can much better safeguard the will of the Congress now that we're in the majority.
Can you give an example?
One of the things the Administration did was to rescind over $500 million in funds for global health. In other words, they cut it, and you had a rubber stamp majority in the Congress. Republicans, go along with that. You would never get Democrats to agree.
There's another ongoing example right now, which is a number of years ago, we passed about $1.5 billion in funds for [global] public health, and it appears that they're using those funds not for public health but to wind down USAID. So this is an area where we could say no, you may not use these funds to wind down USAID.
The administration has been ignoring a lot of these "no's" so far. What gives those "no's" more weight in the majority?
When we in Congress provide a sum of money, for say public health, we say this money should be spent on these specific items, like vaccinations or clinics. That's guidance, that's direction. It's technically called report language, and this report language used to be respected by Democratic and Republican presidents.
The Trump administration has ignored report language because it's not technically legally binding, and Republicans in the Congress have let them get away with it. And the more they let them get away with it, the more they do it.
So we're going to have to convert what used to be report language into real law to prevent this administration from taking those actions. We Democrats have been trying to do that, but since we've been in the minority, we haven't been able to get that passed.
What if the administration still tries to hold up funds or ignore or veto Congress' actions?
This has been a lawless president, and he's still in the White House. But being in the majority will give us more leverage. If we're able to codify the safeguards that would prevent the Trump administration from diverting funds from their intended purpose to something else, that would be legally binding. Then you can go to the courts and say, you know this isn't simply report language. This is not just guidance. This is legally required, and so that does provide the safeguards that we would need.
Now we may have a back and forth and fight with the administration over providing those safeguards, but we're in a much stronger position now than we have been.
If the Democrats win the presidency and keep control of Congress in 2028, would the fate of USAID be revisited? Might the agency return? Or are there parts of the Trump administration's global health policy that you think are worth preserving or building on?
I don't think there's anything the Trump administration has done that's worth preserving or building on. That does not mean that I'm in favor of simply returning to the status quo prior to this administration.
I am a big believer that the role that USAID performed was both helpful to protecting the health of Americans but also helpful to developing good relations with other countries and the people of other countries. I think we need to develop our plan for how we perform this very important role as part of our foreign policy and as part of our health policy. But I'm not saying we would just go back exactly to the way USAID was.

US airlines are canceling thousands of flights after a rare air traffic control outage affected the US.
As of 10:45 p.m. Eastern time on Friday, FlightAware data showed that nearly 7,500 flights to, within, and from the US had been canceled since the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop — meaning no flights could depart — around 3:45 p.m.
The stop was lifted around 8:30 p.m., but after so many cancellations, flight chaos is nearly guaranteed to stretch into the weekend.
If you're wondering what your options are as the terminals pile up with people frantically trying to get a hotel or food voucher — don't rely on your airline to help out.
According to the Department of Transportation, certain delays and cancellations caused by, for example, an ATC outage, are considered "uncontrollable" disruptions.
That means airlines are not required to provide freebies such as hotel stays or food vouchers. Don't confuse the rules with the DoT customer service dashboard, which shows passenger compensation for flights disrupted by controllable factors, such as maintenance or crew scheduling. Pilots or flight attendants timing out due to the outage would not fall under crew scheduling.
Airlines may offer goodwill vouchers to help out affected customers, but don't bank on it. Customers who book their own hotel or other transportation, such as a rental car or train, may be able to get eligible expenses reimbursed by their credit card.
Here's what to do if your flight is disrupted.
1. Know your rights as an airline passenger in the US
According to the Department of Transportation, there is no law requiring US airlines to compensate passengers for disruptions caused by uncontrollable events, such as weather. That also includes air traffic control delays.
The only rule carriers must follow is to refund customers for cancellations, even in cases of uncontrollable events. And that does not mean travel credits or vouchers — it must be to the original form of payment, and includes any add-ons, such as bags or seats.
If you choose to travel but your flight is delayed or canceled, ask the airline for the reason — ideally in writing — so you know what you're entitled to. Airlines have different policies for disruptions they can control.
The DoT's Airline Customer Service Dashboard — launched in 2022 — shows what the 10 largest US airlines promise in those cases, including rebookings, meal vouchers, and hotel accommodations.
2. Monitor your airline's app for rebooking options
When a flight delay or cancellation is announced, expect people to flock to the nearest customer service line for assistance, and for the phone lines to clog.
Wait times can be painfully long, and the best alternatives will likely go quickly. However, some airlines offer the option to rebook on their website or mobile app and waive any fees, making it sometimes easier to make changes online than in person.
If all available options are exhausted, have a plan B, such as waiting to speak with a live agent, contacting the airline through social media, or booking a hotel for the night.
Direct messaging on Facebook or Twitter can actually serve as a virtual placeholder, and you may hear back via chat before speaking to a live agent.
Here are the phone numbers for each airline:
- Alaska: 1-800-252-7522 or text 82008
- Allegiant: 1-702-505-8888
- American: 1-800-433-7300
- Avelo: 1-346-616-9500
- Breeze: No phone number to call, but you can text the airline at 501-273-3931. If you call this number, it'll tell you different ways to contact Breeze, like via email or Facebook Messenger.
- Delta: 1-800-221-1212
- Frontier: No phone number. The best way to contact Frontier is via online chat or email.
- JetBlue: 1-800-538-2583
- Southwest: 1-800-435-9792
- United: 1-800-864-8331
3. Ask for a hotel or meal voucher
For controllable delays or cancellations that result in a customer waiting at least three hours for a new flight or requiring an overnight stay, several airlines will offer meal or hotel vouchers.
Carriers offering both are Alaska Airlines, Allegiant Air, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, Hawaiian Airlines, JetBlue Airways, Southwest Airlines, and United Airlines, per the DoT dashboard.
Frontier Airlines is the only carrier that does not offer accommodations in the event of an overnight delay or cancellation, but it will provide a meal voucher.
For US airlines not listed on the dashboard, or in cases where the disruption is uncontrollable (like because of a winter storm), or if the compensation is unclear, simply ask.
It never hurts to request a meal or hotel during flight disruptions, and you might get lucky with a goodwill gesture from the carrier.
4. Check if your credit card company offers travel insurance
Several major banks offer credit cards with travel insurance, such as Chase's Sapphire Reserve and American Express' Platinum Card. Both offer trip protection, meaning customers who purchased their flights with those cards can benefit.
For example, during a major storm system, many passengers are likely to end up stranded in random cities across the US.
However, banks with travel insurance included can reimburse cardholders for unexpected expenses outside their control, including hotel, meal, and transportation costs.
Travel insurance does not apply in all circumstances, like short delays, so be sure to check your policy before making a claim — but it also doesn't hurt to make the claim anyway, even if the answer is no.
5. Know when to walk away
Delays and cancellations are inevitable. Don't spend all day sitting around waiting — set a cutoff time. Once that moment passes, consider alternative ways to reach your destination, such as driving or taking a bus or train (which may also be covered by travel insurance).
If you are stuck in another city and have no other option but to stay in a hotel or wait at the airport, decide how you want to spend your time and make a plan.

Meta's Muse can now make calls on your behalf (if you have a paid subscription)
The AI agent can schedule appointments, make reservations and wait on hold for you.
Meta's Muse just got another ability that could make the AI agent feel a little bit more like an actual personal assistant. Muse is now able to place phone calls on your behalf, if you have a paid subscription.
With the change, Muse is able to call businesses to help with tasks like making reservations, scheduling appointments and other "calls you don't want to make," Meta's Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said in an update. The feature is available to those who have paid for a separate Muse subscription, which comes with additional tokens and some extra features.
Some users who have had access to the feature already have reported that Muse has been able to handle phone-related tasks with relative ease. Moltbook creator and Meta Superintelligence employee Matt Schlicht shared a recreation of a phone conversation his agent had with a Volvo dealership last month, noting that it was able to wait on hold in order to get the info he needed.
My muse called Volvo for me to see when the next available appointment is.

Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
- Published
The National Basketball Association (NBA) says it removed Rwanda's army team from its African league because of US sanctions imposed on the country in March.
The NBA had previously said the Rwandan army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise (APR) club would not participate in the 2026 Basketball Africa League (BAL).
However this is the first time the NBA has revealed the reasons behind the APR's removal.
The association was responding to complaints by two US senators, who sent a letter asking them to reconsider their partnership with the Rwandan team. The US placed sanctions on the Rwandan army, accusing it of fuelling the conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo in March.
The senators said the NBA risked "becoming complicit in sportswashing by accepting money from a Rwandan government that systematically abuses human rights".
Last week, the US also imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its support for the M23 rebel group which has seized control of large parts of eastern DR Congo. Rwanda denies backing the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.
Rwanda is an official BAL partner and pays the league to host its finals at the 10,000-seat BK Arena in the capital, Kigali.
The BBC has asked Rwanda for comment.

Among other queries, they also questioned how the association could "reconcile its continued partnership with Rwanda with its purported commitment to justice".
In its response, NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum said the Rwandan team "had been withdrawn" from the BAL following the sanctions imposed earlier in the year, American sports website ESPN reports.
